text: 平家皆滅び果てゝ西國も靜まりぬ。國は國司に隨ひ、庄は領家のまゝなり。上下安堵して覺えし程に、同七月九日の午刻許に大地おびたゞしく動て良久し。赤縣の中白河の邊、六勝寺皆破れ壞る。九重の塔も上六重を震落す。得長壽院も三十三間の御堂を十七間まで振倒す。皇居を始めて、人々の家家惣て在々所々の神社佛閣、怪しの民屋、さながら破れ壞るゝ音は雷の如く、揚る塵は烟の如し。天暗うして、日の光も見えず、老少共に魂を銷し、鳥獸悉く心を盡す。又遠國近國もかくのごとし。大地裂て水湧き出で、磐石破て谷へまろぶ。山壞て河を埋み、海漂ひて濱をひたす。汀漕ぐ船は波にゆられ、陸行く駒は足の立處を失へり。洪水みなぎり來らば、岳にのぼてもなどか助ざらん。猛火燃來らば、川を隔ても暫も去ぬべし。唯悲かりけるは大地震也。鳥にあらざれば空をも翔り難く、龍にあらざれば雲にも又上がたし。白河六波羅京中に打埋れて死る者幾等といふ數をしらず。四大種の中に、水火風は常に害をなせども、大地に於ては異なる變をなさず。こは如何にしつる事ぞやとて上下遣戸障子を立て、天の鳴り地の動度毎には、唯今ぞ死ぬるとて聲々に念佛申、をめきさけぶ事おびたゞし。七八十、九十の者も、世の滅するなど云事は、さすが今日明日とはおもはずとて大に噪ぎければ、をさなき者どもも聞て、泣悲しむ事限なし。法皇はその折しも新熊野へ御幸成て、人多く打殺され觸穢出來にければ、急ぎ六波羅へ還御なる。道すがら君も臣もいかばかり御心を碎せ給ひけん。主上は鳳輦に召て、池の汀へ行幸なる。法皇は南庭にあく屋を立てぞましましける。女院宮々は、御所共皆震り倒しければ或は御輿に召し、或は御車に召て、出させ給ふ。天文の博士共馳參て、夕さりの亥子の刻には必ず大地打返すべしと申せば、怖しなども愚也。昔文徳天皇の御宇齊衡三年三月八日の大地震には、東大寺の佛の御ぐしを震落したりけるとかや。又天慶二年四月五日の大地震には、主上御殿を去て、常寧殿の前に五丈のあく屋を立ててましましけるとぞ承る。其は上代の事なれば申におよばず。今度の事は是より後も類あるべしとも覺えず。十善帝王都を出させ給て、御身を海底に沈め、大臣公卿大路を渡して其頸を獄門に懸けらる。昔より今に至るまで怨靈は怖しき事なれば世も如何あらんずらんとて心ある人の歎き悲しまぬは無かりけり。

annotation.translation: The Taira clan was utterly annihilated, and the Western Provinces were quiet. The provinces followed the provincial governors, and the estates remained with the estate lords. Everyone was at ease and felt relieved; however, around noon on the ninth day of the seventh month, the great earth trembled violently for a long time. Within the capital, near Shirakawa, all six胜 temples were broken and destroyed. The nine-story pagoda's upper six stories were shaken down. Detchōjū-in's thirty-three-bay main hall was shaken down to seventeen bays. Starting from the Imperial Palace, all the homes of the people, the various shrines and Buddhist temples in all places, and even strange commoner houses, were all broken and destroyed; the sound was like thunder, and the rising dust was like smoke. The sky grew dark, and the light of the sun could not be seen; young and old alike lost their souls, and birds and beasts all lost their minds. The same happened in distant and nearby provinces. The earth cracked, and water gushed forth; great rocks were broken and rolled into valleys. Mountains collapsed, burying rivers; the sea drifted, submerging the shores. Boats rowing on the water were tossed by the waves; horses traveling on land lost their footing. If a flood came, how could one be saved even by climbing a mountain? If a fierce fire came, how could one depart even for a moment by crossing a river? Only the great earthquake was sorrowful. If one is not a bird, it is difficult to fly in the sky; if one is not a dragon, it is impossible to rise into the clouds. In Shirakawa, Rokuhara, and within the capital, countless people were buried and died; their number is unknown. Among the four great elements, fire, water, and wind always cause harm, but the earth does not usually produce such strange changes. What could have caused this? People everywhere closed their sliding doors and windows; at every sound from the heavens and every tremor of the earth, they cried out, "Now we will die!" and chanted the nembutsu; wailing and screaming were countless. Even those in their seventies, eighties, nineties, and beyond, who had never thought that the world would end so soon, began to make a great noise; when the younger people heard this, they wept and lamented without limit. At that very time, the retired Emperor went on a pilgrimage to the new Kumano; many people were killed and defiled, so he hurriedly returned to Rokuhara. Along the way, how much grief must the Emperor and his ministers have felt! The reigning Emperor was summoned into the phoenix palanquin and went to the shore of the pond. The retired Emperor erected a temporary hut in the southern garden. The Empress Dowager and the princesses, finding their palaces all shaken and collapsed, were either carried in palanquins or in carriages and were taken out. Scholars of astronomy rushed to attend and said that at the hour of the pig at sunset on the evening of that day, the great earth would certainly turn over again; such fear was foolish. Was it not the case that during the great earthquake of the eighth day of the third month of the third year of Saikō, in the reign of Emperor Monmu, the Buddha's pillar of Tōdai-ji was shaken down? I have also heard that during the great earthquake of the fifth day of the fourth month of the second year of Tenkyō, the reigning Emperor left his palace and erected a five-jō high temporary hut before the Jōei-dō. Since those were events of former reigns, they need not be mentioned. This time, however, I do not sense that such events will occur in the future. The ten-good Emperor ordered the capital to be abandoned, and he sank his body into the sea; the great ministers and high nobles crossed the main road, and their necks were hung on the prison gate. Since spirits of the resentful dead have always been terrifying from ancient times to the present, the world must be in some state of turmoil; thus, no person with a heart did not sigh and lament.

text: 同八月廿二日、鎌倉の源二位頼朝卿の父故左馬頭義朝のうるはしき頭とて、高雄の文覺上人頸にかけ、鎌田兵衞が頸をば、弟子が頸にかけさせて、鎌倉へぞ下られける。去治承四年の比取出して、たてまつりけるは實の左馬頭の首にはあらず。謀反をすゝめ奉らんためのはかりごとに、そぞろなるふるい頭をしろい布に包んでたてまつりけるに、謀反を起し、世を討取て、一向父の頭と信ぜられける處へ又尋出してくだりけり。是は年來義朝の不便にして召使はれける紺掻の男、年來獄門に懸られて後世弔ふ人も無りし事をかなしんで時の大理に逢ひ奉り申給はり取おろして、兵衞佐殿流人でおはすれども、末たのもしき人なり。もし世に出でて尋ねらるゝ事もこそあれとて東山圓覺寺といふ所に、深う納めて置きたりけるを、文覺聞出して、彼紺掻男共に、相具して下りけるとかや。今日既に鎌倉へ著くと聞えしかば、源二位片瀬河まで迎におはしけり。其より色の姿に成て、泣々鎌倉へ入給ふ。聖をば大床に立て、我身は庭に立て、父の頭を請取り給ふぞ哀なる。是を見る大名小名、皆涙を流さずと云事なし。せき巖の峻しきを伐掃て、新なる道場を造り、父の御爲と供養して、勝長壽院と號せらる。公家にもか樣の事を哀と思食て、故左馬頭義朝の墓へ、内大臣正二位を贈らる。勅使は左大辨兼忠とぞ聞えし。頼朝卿武勇の名譽長ぜるによて、身を立て家を興すのみならず、亡父聖靈、贈官贈位に及けるこそ目出たけれ。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-second day of the eighth month of that year, the beautiful head of the late Minister of the Left of Kamakura, the Lord Gen no Ni, Yoritomo, who was the father of the late Minister of the Left Yoshitomo, was hung upon the neck of the ascetic Bunkaku of Takao, and the neck of the soldier Kanda Heizaemon was hung upon the neck of his disciple, and they descended to Kamakura. It was not the head of the real Minister of the Left, which had been taken out and presented in the fourth year of Jishō. It was a head of long ago that had been secretly wrapped in white cloth and presented in order to encourage rebellion; when he rose in rebellion and sought to overthrow the world, he was believed to be his father's head, but it was again discovered. This was the blue-patterned man who had served Yoshitomo for years as an inconvenient retainer, who had been hanged on the gallows for years and for whom there was no one to mourn him in the afterlife; pitying this, he met the Minister of the Left at that time, and by the Emperor's command, he was taken down. Although he was an exile in the Kanda Heizaemon domain, he was a person of great promise. Thinking that he might be sought after if he appeared in the world, he had deeply concealed him at a place called Engaku-ji on Higashiyama. Bunkaku discovered him, and together with that blue-patterned man, they descended. When it was heard today that he had already arrived in Kamakura, the Lord Gen no Ni went to meet him as far as Katakase River. From there, he became a figure of color and tears, entering Kamakura. The Emperor stood on the great platform, he himself stood in the garden, and he received his father's head; this was most moving. All the great and minor lords who saw this shed tears without exception. They cleared away the steep rocks and built a new dojo, and for the sake of his father, they performed memorial services and named it Shōchōju-in. Even the court nobles felt such sorrow, and they posthumously bestowed the title of Minister of the Interior, Junior Second Rank, upon the late Minister of the Left Yoshitomo. The imperial envoy was said to be Sada no Daigen, Kanetada. Because the Lord Yoritomo's reputation for military valor had grown, not only did he establish himself and revive his family, but it was especially auspicious that his deceased father's holy spirit was even granted official rank and posthumous titles.

text: 同九月二十三日、平家の餘黨の都にあるを、國々へ遣はさるべき由鎌倉殿より公家へ申されたりければ、平大納言時忠卿能登國、子息讃岐中將時實上總國、内藏頭信基安藝國、兵部少輔正明隱岐國、二位僧都專親阿波國、法勝寺執行能圓備後國、中納言律師忠快武藏國とぞ聞えし。或西海の波の上、或東關の雲の果て、先途何くを期せず、後會其期を知らず、別の涙を押て、面々に赴かれけん心の中推量れて哀なり。其中に平大納言は、建禮門院の吉田に渡らせ給ふ處に參て「時忠こそ責重うして、今日既に配所へ趣き候へ。同じ都の内に候て、御當りの御事共承はらまほしう候つるに、終に如何なる御有樣にて渡らせ給ひ候はんずらむと、思置參せ候にこそ、行空も覺ゆまじう候へ。」と、泣々申されければ、女院、「げにも昔の名殘とては、そこばかりこそおはしつれ。今はあはれをもかけ、吊ふ人も誰かは有るべき。」とて御涙せきあへさせ給はず。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-third day of the same ninth month, it was reported to the courtiers from the Lord of Kamakura that the remaining forces of the Taira clan in the capital should be dispatched to various provinces. It was heard that Minister of the Left Taira no Tokitada was to be sent to Noto Province, his son, the Captain of the Left Guards Taira no Tokazane to Satsuma Province, the Chamberlain Nobemoto to Aki Province, the Vice-Minister of the Ministry of War Masaki to Oki Province, the Second Rank Monk Abbot Senkin to Awaji Province, the Head Priest of Hossō-ji Nōen to Bitchū Province, and the Vice-Minister of the Left and Buddhist Preceptor Tadao to Musashi Province. Some were to the waves of the Western Sea, some to the ends of the clouds of the Eastern Pass; not knowing the destination of their journey, nor the time of their future meeting, they pressed back their tears and departed one by one, a sight most pitiable to behold. Among them, Minister of the Left Taira no Tokitada went to the place where the Empress Dowager of Kenrei-mon-in was crossing to Yoshida, and with tears in his eyes said: 'Tokitada, though heavily burdened with blame, has already departed today to his place of exile. I had hoped to remain in the capital and receive your lordship's instructions, but I wonder what kind of appearance you will take upon yourself as you depart. I thought you would not depart, yet you have gone.' Upon hearing this, the Empress Dowager said, 'Indeed, in the past, you might have lingered as a remnant of old times, but now, who would have any compassion or sympathy for you?' and she could not hold back her tears.

text: 此大納言と申は、出羽前司具信が孫、兵部權大輔贈左大臣時信が子也。故建春門院の御せうとにて高倉の上皇の御外戚なり。世の覺え時のきら目出たかりき。入道相國の北方、八條の二位殿も姉にておはせしかば、兼官兼職、思の如く心の如し。されば程なくあがて正二位の大納言に至れり。檢非違使別當にも三箇度までなり給ふ。此人の廳務の時は、竊盗強盗をば召捕て、樣もなく右のかひなをば腕中より打落し／＼追捨らる。されば惡別當とぞ申ける。主上併三種の神器都へ返し入奉るべき由西國へ院宣を下されたりけるに院宣の御使、花形がつらに、浪形と云燒驗をせられけるも、此大納言のしわざ也。法皇も故女院の御せうとなれば、御形見に御覽ぜまほしう思召しけれども、加樣の惡行によて御憤淺からず。九郎判官も親しうなられたりしかば、いかにもして申宥めばやと思はれけれども叶はず。子息侍從時家とて、十六になられけるが流罪にも漏れて、伯父の時光卿の許におはしけり。母上帥のすけ殿の共に、大納言の袂にすがり、袖をひかへて今を限りの名殘をぞ惜みける。大納言、「終にすまじき別かは。」と心強は宣へどもさこそは悲しうも思はれけめ。年闌齡傾て後、さしも睦まじかりし妻子にも、別果て、住慣し都をも、雲井の餘所に顧みて、古へは名にのみ聞し越路の旅に趣き、遙々と下り給ふに、彼は志賀唐崎、是は眞野の入江、交田の浦と申ければ、大納言泣々詠じ給ひけり。

annotation.translation: This Great Councilor is the grandson of Toshiyori, former Governor of Dewa, and the son of Tokinori, who was posthumously promoted to Minister of the Left while serving as Vice-Minister of the Ministry of War. Thus, he was a maternal cousin of the retired Empress Kenshunmon and a maternal uncle of the retired Emperor Takakura. In his time, he was a brilliant and celebrated figure. Since his wife, the Northern Lady of the Great Minister (Daijō-daijin), and Lady Ni no Miya of the Eight-Street also were his sisters, he enjoyed all the official posts and titles he desired. Consequently, within a short time, he rose to the rank of Senior Second Rank and Great Councilor. He also served as the Governor of the Gionji Office no fewer than three times. During his tenure as Governor, he would arrest thieves and robbers, and without any regard for their status, would strike them down from their shoulders and beat them mercilessly. Therefore, he was known as the Wicked Governor. When the Emperor was ordered by an imperial edict to send the Three Sacred Treasures back to the capital along with the retired Emperor to the western provinces, the imperial envoy, who was a descendant of the flower-patterned lineage, was subjected to the trial by fire known as 'Nami-gata' (Wave-pattern), yet this was the doing of this Great Councilor. Since the retired Emperor was also a maternal cousin of the late retired Empress, he wished to view his heirloom, but his many wicked acts caused the Emperor's anger to be far from mild. Even though Kurogo no Shōgen had become close to him, he considered how he might beg for forgiveness, but it was impossible. His son, the Junior Assistant Councilor Tokiie, had reached the age of sixteen but was also exiled to a remote province, and he went to reside at the residence of his uncle, Tokitoki. His mother, Lady Sukeno, daughter of the Commander's Assistant, clung to the Great Councilor's sleeve, holding it, and sorrowfully mourned parting with him. The Great Councilor, though he bravely declared, 'This is indeed a parting that cannot be endured,' surely felt deep sorrow. After his age had waned and his prime had passed, even though he had been so close to his wife and children, he finally parted from them. Turning his gaze from the capital he had long called home to a distant place beyond the clouds, he set out on a journey to the Koshu region, which he had only heard of by name in ancient times, and descended far and wide. There, he visited Shiga-no-Tōzaki, this was Mino-no-Irie, and Kōda-no-Ura, and the Great Councilor, weeping, composed a poem.

When the Emperor was ordered by an imperial edict to send the Three Sacred Treasures back to the capital along with the retired Emperor to the western provinces, the imperial envoy, who was a descendant of the flower-patterned lineage, was subjected to the trial by fire known as 'Nami-gata' (Wave-pattern), yet this was the doing of this Great Councilor. Since the retired Emperor was also a maternal cousin of the late retired Empress, he wished to view his heirloom, but his many wicked acts caused the Emperor's anger to be far from mild. Even though Kurogo no Shōgen had become close to him, he considered how he might beg for forgiveness, but it was impossible. His son, the Junior Assistant Councilor Tokiie, had reached the age of sixteen but was also exiled to a remote province, and he went to reside at the residence of his uncle, Tokitoki. His mother, Lady Sukeno, daughter of the Commander's Assistant, clung to the Great Councilor's sleeve, holding it, and sorrowfully mourned parting with him. The Great Councilor, though he bravely declared, 'This is indeed a parting that cannot be endured,' surely felt deep sorrow. After his age had waned and his prime had passed, even though he had been so close to his wife and children, he finally parted from them. Turning his gaze from the capital he had long called home to a distant place beyond the clouds, he set out on a journey to the Koshu region, which he had only heard of by name in ancient times, and descended far and wide. There, he visited Shiga-no-Tōzaki, this was Mino-no-Irie, and Kōda-no-Ura, and the Great Councilor, weeping, composed a poem.

text: 昨日は西海の波の上に漂ひて、怨憎會苦の恨を扁舟の内に積み、今日は北國の雪の下に埋れて、愛別離苦の悲みを故郷の雲に重ねたり。

annotation.translation: Yesterday, I drifted upon the waves of the Western Sea, loading the resentment of the bitterness of meeting with those I hate into my small boat; today, I am buried beneath the snow of the Northern Land, piling the sorrow of the bitterness of parting from those I love upon the clouds of my homeland.

text: さる程に九郎判官には鎌倉殿より大名十人つけられたりけれども、内々御不審を蒙り給ふ由聞えしかば、心を合せて一人づつ皆下り果にけり。兄弟なる上、殊に父子の契をして去年の正月木曾義仲を追討せしより以降度々平家を攻落し、今年の春滅し果てゝ一天を靜め、四海を澄す。勸賞行はるべき所に、如何なる仔細有て、かゝる聞えあるらんと、上一人を始め奉り下萬民に至るまで、不審をなす。此事は、去春攝津國渡邊より舟汰して八島へ渡り給ひし時、逆櫓立うたてじの論をして、大きに欺かれたりしを、梶原遺恨に思ひて常は讒言しけるに依て也。定て謀反の心もあるらん。大名共差上せば、宇治勢田の橋をも引き、京中の噪ぎと成て、中々惡かりなんとて土佐房正俊を召て「和僧上て、物詣する樣にてたばかり討て。」と宣ひければ正俊畏て承り、宿所へも歸らず、御前を立て軈て京へぞ上りける。

annotation.translation: In such a manner, although Ten Great Lords were assigned to Shichiro-no-kami from the Lord of Kamakura, hearing that he had privately received the Emperor's suspicions, they united their hearts and one by one all departed, completing their exit. Being brothers, and especially bound by the father-son bond since last New Year when they were ordered to pursue and destroy Kiso Yoshinaka, they repeatedly attacked and brought down the Taira family; this spring they utterly destroyed them, pacified the realm, and cleared the four seas. Where reward and praise should be given, what could possibly be the reason for such reports? From the one above to the myriad below, they harbor suspicions. This matter arose because, when he went by boat from Watanabe in Settsu Province to Yashima last spring, he was greatly deceived in the argument about setting the oars against the current; thus Kajiwara, holding a grudge, constantly slandered him, and this is the cause. There surely must be thoughts of rebellion. If the great lords are summoned, they may pull even the bridge at Uji-Seta and turn the capital into a hub of uproar, which would be terribly bad; therefore, he summoned Tosano-fusa Masatoshi and declared, 'Go up to the temple as if making a pilgrimage for worship, and kill him.' Fearing this, Masatoshi accepted the order, did not return to his lodging, and quickly ascended to the capital to stand before the Emperor.

text:
同九月廿九日土佐房都へついたりけれ共、次の日迄判官殿へもまゐらず。土佐房がのぼりたる由聞給ひ、武藏房辨慶を以て召されければ、やがてつれて參りたり。判官宣ひけるは、「如何に鎌倉殿より御文はなきか。」「指たる御事候はぬ間、御文はまゐらせられず候。『御詞にて申せ。』と候ひしは『當時まで都に別の仔細無く候事、さて御渡候故と覺え候。相構てよく守護せさせ給へ。と申せ。』とこそ仰せられ候つ
れ。」判官、「よもさはあらじ、義經討に上る御使なり。大名ども差上せば、宇治勢
田の橋をも引き都の噪ぎとも成て、中々惡かりなん。和僧上せて物詣する樣にて、た
ばかて討てとぞ仰附られたるらんな。」と宣へば、正俊大に驚て、「何に依てか、唯
今さる事の候べき。聊宿願に依て熊野参詣の爲に罷上て候。」其時判官宣ひけるは、
「景時が讒言に依て義經鎌倉へもいれられず、見參をだにし給はで追上せらるゝ事は
如何に。」正俊「其事は如何候らん、身においては全く御後ぐらう候はず。起請文を
書き進らすべき」由申せば。判官「とてもかうても、鎌倉殿によしと思はれ奉たらば
こそ。」とて、以外氣色惡しげに成り給ふ。正俊一旦の害をのがれんがために居なが
ら七枚の起請文を書て或は燒て飮み、或は社に納などして、ゆりて歸り、大番衆に觸
回して其夜やがて寄せんとす。判官は磯禪師といふ白拍子の娘しづかと云女を最愛せ
られけり。しづかも傍を立去る事なし。しづか申けるは、「大路は皆武者で候ふなる。
是より催の無らんに、大番衆の者どもの是程噪ぐべき樣やさぶらふ。あはれ是は晝の起請法師のしわざと覺え候。人を遣して見せさぶらはばや。」とて、六波羅の故入道相國の召使かはれける禿を三四人使はれけるを、二人遣したりけるが、程ふるまで歸らず。中々女は苦しからじとて半者を一人見せに遣す。程なく走り歸て申けるは、「禿と覺しきものは、二人ながら土佐房の門に切伏られて候。宿所には鞍おき馬ども、ひしと引立て、大幕の内には、矢負、弓張、者共皆具足して唯今寄んと出立候ふ。少も物詣の景色とは見え候はず。」と申ければ、判官是を聞いてやがて討立給ふ。靜著背長取て投懸奉る。高紐計して、太刀取て出給へば、中門の前に馬に鞍置て引立たり、是に打乘て「門を開よ。」とて門あけさせ、今や／＼と待給ふ處に、暫有て直甲四五十騎門の前に推寄せて、閧をどとぞ作ける。判官鐙蹈張り立あがり、大音聲をあげて、「夜討にも晝戰にも、義經たやすう討つべき者は、日本國にはおぼえぬものを。」とて只一騎おめいて懸け給へば、五十騎ばかりの者共中をあけてぞ通しける。さる程に、江田源三、熊井太郎、武藏坊辨慶など云一人當千の兵共、やがて續いて責戰ふ。其後侍共御内に夜討入たりとて、あそこの屋形、爰の宿所より駈來る。程なく六七十騎集ければ、土佐房猛く寄たりけれども、戰に及ばず、散々に懸散されて扶かる者はすくなう、討るゝ者ぞ多かりける。正俊希有にしてそこをばのがれて鞍馬の奧ににげ籠りたりけるが、鞍馬は判官の故山なりければ、彼法師土佐房を搦めて、次日判官の許へ送りけり。僧正が谷と云所に隱れ居たりけるとかや。正俊を大庭に引居たり。かちの直垂にすちやう頭巾をぞしたりける。判官笑て宣ひけるは「いかに和僧、起請にはうてたるぞ。」土佐房少しも噪がず、居なほりあざ笑て申けるは。「ある事に書て候へば、うてて候ぞかし。」と申す。「主君の命を重んじて、私の命を輕んず、志の程最神妙也。和僧命惜くば、鎌倉へかへし遣さんはいかに。」土佐房、「正なうも御諚候者哉。惜しと申さば、殿は扶け給はんずるか。鎌倉殿の、法師なれども、己ぞねらはんずる者とて、仰蒙しより、命をば鎌倉殿に奉りぬ。なじかは取返奉るべき。只御恩には疾々頭を召され候へ。」と申ければ、「さらばきれ。」とて、六條河原に引出て切てげり。褒めぬ人こそ無りけれ。

annotation.translation: On the 29th day of the ninth month, he arrived in the capital, but did not go to the Lord Gongen until the next day. When they heard that Tosano had ascended, they summoned Musashibō Benkei, who immediately took him there. The Lord Gongen asked, 'Why is there no letter from Lord Kamakura?' 'Because the matter of the letter has not been decided, no letter has been sent. He said, "Speak in your own words." He added, "Until now, there has been no special reason to stay in the capital; since you are now returning, you should be well guarded." Thus he instructed.' The Lord Gongen said, 'There is no way that is true; he is an envoy sent to hunt down Yoshitsune. If the great lords send him, even Uji no Hashi could become a place of uproar in the capital, and it would be extremely dangerous. He was instructed to appear as if going on a pilgrimage to Kumano, and then to attack him.' When he said this, Masatoshi was greatly startled and said, 'Why would such a thing happen now? It is merely because I went on a pilgrimage to Kumano out of a long-held vow.' At that time, the Lord Gongen asked, 'Because of Jitsunō's slander, Yoshitsune was not allowed to enter Kamakura, and he was chased without even being granted an audience. How could this be?' Masatoshi replied, 'As for that matter, I am completely free from any blame. I should write and submit a formal oath.' The Lord Gongen said, 'Even if you do so, it must be accepted by Lord Kamakura.' With this, he suddenly became extremely angry. To avoid immediate danger, Masatoshi stayed there, wrote seven oaths, burned some and drank them, or deposited some in temples, then left and, after passing through the guards, intended to return that very night. The Lord Gongen loved a white-robed girl named Shizuka, a biwa player. Shizuka never left his side. She said, 'The main road is full of warriors. It seems strange that the guards are making such a commotion now, when there is no festival. I suspect this is the work of the monk who took the oath. If we send someone to investigate, what do you think?' She sent two or three of the former servants of the retired Lord of Rokuhara, but they did not return for a long time. Not wanting the women to suffer further, she sent one more. Soon, the messenger ran back and reported, 'Those who appeared to be monks were ambushed and cut down at Tosano's gate. At the lodging, horses with saddles were being dragged together in a crowd. Inside the great tent, all the men were fully armed with bows and arrows, and they were preparing to attack at this very moment. There was no sign of a pilgrimage.' When the Lord Gongen heard this, he immediately prepared to fight. Shizuka tied her hair back, donned armor, and handed him his sword. He mounted a horse that was waiting with its saddle before the inner gate, rode out, and commanded, 'Open the gate!' As he waited, soon forty or fifty armored riders pushed forward before the gate and made a loud clamor. The Lord Gongen stepped into his stirrups, stood up, and shouted in a loud voice, 'Whether it is a night attack or a daytime battle, there is no one in the Land of Japan who can easily defeat Yoshitsune!' He then charged alone on his horse, and the fifty or so riders parted to let him pass. Shortly after, warriors such as Eida Genzō, Kumai Tarō, and Musashibō Benkei, renowned as one man capable of facing a thousand, followed and attacked. Afterward, the samurai came running from the nearby houses and lodgings, saying that a night attack had entered the inner quarters. Soon sixty or seventy riders gathered. Although Tosano attacked fiercely, they did not engage in battle; they were scattered in disorder, and few were able to support each other, while many were killed. Masatoshi, with great difficulty, escaped from there and fled into the depths of Kurama. Since Kurama was the former mountain of the Lord Gongen, that monk captured Tosano and sent him to the Lord Gongen the next day. It is said that he hid in a place called Sōjō no Tani. Masatoshi was brought to the courtyard. He wore a plain robe and a simple head covering. The Lord Gongen laughed and said, 'How strange, monk, that you were killed while taking an oath.' Tosano made no sound, sat calmly, and mocked him, saying, 'Since I wrote it for a certain purpose, I was killed.' The Lord Gongen said, 'You value my master's life more than your own; your determination is truly profound. If you wish to save your life, I could send you back to Kamakura. What do you say?' Tosano replied, 'It is truly a noble thought. If I were to say I wish to live, would His Excellency save me? Lord Kamakura, though I am a monk, sought to kill me; therefore, I have offered my life to Lord Kamakura. How could I take it back? I only ask that you accept my gratitude and take my head quickly.' Hearing this, the Lord Gongen said, 'Very well,' and had him dragged out to the Rokujō River and beheaded. There was no one who did not praise this act.'

text: ここに足立新三郎といふ雜色は、「きやつは下臈なれども、以外さか／＼しいやつで候。召使ひ給へ。」とて、判官に參せられたりけるが「内々九郎が振舞見て、我に知せよ。」とぞ宣ひける。正俊がきらるゝを見て、新三郎夜を日についではせ下り、鎌倉殿に此由申ければ、舍弟參河守範頼を、討手に上せ給ふべき由仰られけり。頻に辭申されけれども、重て仰られける間、力及ばで物具して、暇申に參られたり。「わ殿も九郎がまねし給ふなよ。」と仰られければ、此御詞に恐れて、物具脱置て京上はとどまり給ひぬ。全く不忠なき由一日に十枚づゝの起請を晝は書き、夜は御坪の内にて讀上讀あげ百日に千枚の起請を書て參らせられたりけれども、叶はずして終に討たれ給ひけり。其後北條四郎時政を大將として討手のぼると聞えしかば、判官殿鎭西の方へ落ばやと思ひ立ち給ふ處に緒方三郎維義は平家を九國の内へも入奉らず、逐出す程の威勢の者なりければ、判官「我に憑まれよ。」と宣ひける。「さ候はば、御内に候菊池次郎高直は、年來の敵で候。給はて頸を切て憑まれ參らせん。」と申。左右なくたうだりければ、六條河原に引出して切てげり。其後維義かひ／＼しう領状す。

annotation.translation: Here is Ashikaga Shinsaburo, a servant, who said, "Although I am a lowly servant, I am a remarkable fellow; please employ me." And so he was sent to the Daimon, who said, "Watch the behavior of the Ninth Lord and report to me." Seeing that Masatoshi was dissatisfied, Shinsaburo, day and night, hastened down and reported this to the Lord of Kamakura, who ordered that his younger brother, Sagami-no-kami Noriyori, be appointed as the leader of the troops to attack. Although Shinsaburo frequently made excuses, he was ordered repeatedly, and unable to resist, he prepared himself and reported to the Daimon. When he was told, "Even the Lord will not follow the Ninth Lord's example," he, fearing these words, abandoned his preparations and remained in Kyoto. He wrote ten petitions each day, reading them aloud during the day and in the inner courtyard at night, and after one hundred days, he submitted a thousand petitions, but it was in vain, and he was finally killed. Afterward, when he heard that Hojo Shiro Tokimasa was being appointed as the general of the attacking troops, the Daimon, thinking of fleeing to the western province of Chikuzen, encountered Ogata Saburo Yoroyoshi, who was a man of such authority that he would not allow the Taira family even to enter the nine provinces and would drive them out. The Daimon said, "Rely on me." Yoroyoshi replied, "If that be the case, Kikuchi Jiro Takanao, who is my lifelong enemy, is in your inner court. I shall be given the chance to cut off his head and rely on you." With no hesitation, he drew him out at Rokyogawara and beheaded him. Afterward, Yoroyoshi became increasingly powerful and issued charters.

text: 同十一月二日、九郎大夫判官院御所へ參て、大藏卿泰經朝臣を以て、奏聞しけるは「義經君の御爲に奉公の忠を致す事、事あたらしう始て申上るに及候はず。しかるを頼朝、郎等共が讒言に依て、義經をうたんと仕候間暫く鎭西の方へ罷下らばやと存候。院の廳の御下文を一通下預候ばや。」[1]と申されけれは、法皇「此條頼朝がかへり聞かん事いかゞあるべからん。」とて諸卿に仰合られければ、「義經都に候て關東の大勢亂入候はゞ京都の狼藉絶え候べからず。遠國へ下候なば暫く其恐あらず。」とおの／＼一同に申されければ、緒方三郎をはじめて、臼杵、戸次、松浦黨、惣じて鎭西の者共義經を大將として其下知にしたがふべき由廳の御下文を給はてければ、其勢五百餘騎明る三日卯刻に京都に聊の煩も成さず、波風も立てずして下りにけり。攝津の國源氏、太田太郎頼基、「我門の前を通しながら矢一つ射懸で有るべきか。」とて、河原津と云ふ所に追著て責戰ふ。判官は五百餘騎、太田太郎は六十餘騎にて有ければ、中に取籠め「餘すな泄すな。」とて散々に攻給へば、太田太郎吾身も手負ひ、家子郎等多く討せ、馬の腹射させて引退く。判官頸共切り懸けて、軍神に祭り、「門出好し。」と悦で大物浦より船に乘て下られけるが、折節西の風烈しく吹き住吉の浦に打上られて、吉野の奧にぞ籠りける。吉野法師にせめられて、奈良へ落つ。奈良法師にせめられて、又都へ歸り入、北國にかゝて終に奧へぞ下られける。都より相具したりける女房達十餘人、住吉の浦に捨置きたれば、松の下、砂の上に袴蹈しだき、袖を片敷て泣臥したりけるを、住吉の神官共あはれんで、皆京へぞ送りける。凡判官の憑まれたりける伯父信太三郎先生義教、十郎藏人行家、緒方三郎維義が船共、浦々島々に打寄せられて、互に其行末をしらず。忽に西の風吹ける事も、平家の怨靈の故とぞおぼえける。同十一月七日鎌倉の源二位頼朝卿の代官として北條四郎時政、六萬餘騎を相具して都へ入。明る八日院參して伊豫守源義經、備前守同行家、信太三郎先生同義教、追討すべき由奏聞しければやがて院宣を下されけり。去二日は、義經が申請る旨に任せて、頼朝を背べき由廳の御下文成され、同八日は、頼朝卿の申状に依て、義經追討の院宣を下さる。朝にかはり夕に變ずる世間の不定こそ哀なれ。

annotation.translation: On the same day, the second day of the eleventh month, [he] went to the Imperial Palace of the Nine-Rank Grand Councilor, and, taking Ootonomiya Yasunori, a Court Noble, as a messenger, reported: "It is a matter of great urgency to serve Lord Yoshitsune with loyalty; this is the first time I have been able to submit such a report. However, since Yoritomo, influenced by the slander of his retainers, intends to kill Yoshitsune, I am considering that it would be advisable to temporarily go down to the Chikuzen region. If the Imperial Office were to issue an official document for this purpose, it would be ideal." When this was said, the Emperor remarked to the various ministers, "How can Yoritomo be unaware of this matter?" The ministers then replied in unison, "If Yoshitsune remains in the capital and the eastern forces invade, the chaos in Kyoto will never cease. If he goes down to a distant province, there will be no fear for a time." Consequently, from Ogata Saburo onward, the forces of Usuki, Tsutsuki, Matsura, and all the people of Chikuzen were commanded by the Imperial Office to follow Yoshitsune as their general. With a force of over five hundred cavalry, they descended on the third day at dawn, without causing any trouble or raising a ripple in the capital. In the province of Settsu, Minamoto Tarō Yorimochi of the Minamoto clan said, "Is it acceptable for them to pass right by our gates without firing even a single arrow?" He pursued them to a place called Kawarazutsu and engaged them in battle. Since the Councilor had over five hundred cavalry and Minamoto Tarō had over sixty, they were surrounded and attacked relentlessly with the cry, "Do not let any escape!" Minamoto Tarō was wounded himself, many of his retainers were killed, and his horses were shot in the belly, forcing him to retreat. The Councilor cut off their heads and worshipped them as the God of War, saying, "A good departure," and in great joy, he boarded a boat from the great Oomura and descended. However, just at that moment, a strong west wind blew, driving them to the shore of Sumiyoshi, where they retreated into the depths of Yoshino. They were attacked by the Yoshino monks and fell back to Nara. They were attacked by the Nara monks and returned to the capital, then finally descended to the northern provinces. Over ten ladies-in-waiting who had accompanied them from the capital were abandoned at Sumiyoshi Bay; they walked barefoot on the sand beneath the pine trees, spread their sleeves, and wept while lying down. The priests of the Sumiyoshi shrine, pitying them, sent them all back to Kyoto. The ships of the Councilor's uncles, Shinta Saburo Yoshinori, Juro Kurando Yukiie, and Ogata Saburo Ieyoshi, were scattered across various bays and islands, and no one knew their fate. It seemed as though the sudden west wind was the result of the vengeful spirits of the Taira clan. On the seventh day of the same eleventh month, Hōjō Shigemasa, acting as the deputy of Minamoto no Yoritō, the Second Rank of Kamakura, entered the capital with over sixty thousand cavalry. On the eighth day, the Emperor attended the Imperial Palace, and when it was reported that Minamoto no Yoshitsune, Governor of Iyo, Minamoto no Yukiie, Governor of Bizen, and Shinta Saburo Yoshinori should be pursued and punished, an imperial decree was immediately issued. On the second day, a directive from the Imperial Office was issued, stating that Yoritō should be opposed according to Yoshitsune's petition. On the eighth day, following Yoritō's submission, an imperial decree was issued to pursue and punish Yoshitsune. The impermanence of the world, where morning turns to evening, is truly sorrowful.

text: さる程に、鎌倉殿日本國の惣追捕使を給はて、段別に兵粮米を宛行ふべき由、申されければ、「昔より朝の怨敵を亡したる者は半國を給はるといふ事、無量義經に見えたり。されども吾朝にはいまだ其例なし。是は頼朝が過分の申状なり。」と法皇仰なりけれども、公卿僉議あて、「頼朝卿の申さるる處道理半なり。」とて諸卿一同に申されければ、御許されありけるとかや。諸國に守護を置き、庄園に地頭を補せらる。一毛許も隱べき樣なかりけり。鎌倉殿か樣の事、公家にも人多しといへども吉田大納言經房卿をもて奏聞せられけり。此大納言は、うるはしい人と聞え給へり。平家に結ぼほれたりし人々も、源氏の世の強りし後は或文を下し、或使者を遣し、樣々諂ひ給ひしかども、此人はさもし給はず。されば平家の時も法皇を鳥羽殿に押籠參せて後院の別當を置かれしにも、勘解由小路中納言、此經房卿二人をぞ後院の別當には成されたりける。權右中辨光房朝臣の子也。十二の年、父の朝臣失せ給ひしかば、孤にておはせしかども、次第に昇進滯らず、三事の顯要を兼帶して、夕郎の貫首を經、參議、大辨、太宰帥正二位大納言に至れり。人をば越給へ共、人には越られ給はず。されば人の善惡は、錐嚢をとほすとて遂に隱なし。有がたかりし人なり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, the Lord of Kamakura was appointed as the Grand Inspector of the Realm of Japan, and it was reported that military rations should be allocated by grade. 'Since ancient times, it is recorded in the Muryogi Sutra that those who have destroyed the Emperor's mortal enemies are granted half the country. However, in our court, such an example has never occurred. This is Lord Yoritomo's excessive petition,' the Retired Emperor declared. Yet, when all the court nobles deliberated together, they stated, 'Lord Yoritomo's petition is half-right in reason.' Thus, it was reported to all the nobles that it was permitted. Guardians were appointed in the provinces, and stewards were installed in the estates and manors; there was no way for anything to be hidden. Although Lord Kamakura's affairs were widely known even among the court nobles, the Great Counselor Yoshida no Tadanobu was chosen to report to the throne. This Great Counselor was heard to be a handsome man. Even those who had allied with the Taira, after the rise of the Minamoto, sent various documents or sent various messengers to flatter him, but he did not flatter them in return. Therefore, even when the Taira period had the Emperor confined to the Toba Palace and the Abbot of the Rear Palace was appointed, it was the two, the Chūnagon Kanjōji and this Counselor Tadanobu, who were made the Abbots of the Rear Palace. He was the son of the Right Middle Recorder Mitsufusa no Ason. When he was twelve years old, his father, the Ason, passed away, and though he was an orphan, he advanced steadily without delay, holding multiple important offices, serving as the Chief of the Evening Secretaries, and rising through the positions of San'i, Great Recorder, and Dazai no Sochi to become the Second Rank Great Counselor. Though he surpassed others, others could not surpass him. Therefore, regarding a person's good or evil, as the saying goes, 'the awl in the bag will eventually pierce through,' nothing could be hidden. He was a most remarkable person.

text: 北條四郎策に「平家の子孫といはん人、尋出したらん輩に於ては、所望請ふに依べし。」と披露せらる。京中の者共案内は知たり、「勸賞蒙らん。」とて、尋求るぞうたてき。かゝりければ、幾等も尋出したりけり。下臈の子なれども、色白う眉目好きをば召し出いて「是はなんの中將殿の若君、彼少將殿の君達。」と申せば、父母泣悲めども、「あれは介錯が申候、あれは乳母が申。」なんど云ふ間、無下にをさなきをば水に入、土に埋み、少し長しきをば押殺し、刺殺す。母の悲み乳母が歎き喩へん方ぞ無りける。北條も子孫さすが多ければ、是をいみじとは思はねど、世に隨ふ習なれば、力及ばず。

annotation.translation: Hojo Shiro-saku announced, "As for those who claim to be descendants of the Taira clan, they should be investigated and, if found, dealt with as requested." The people of Kyoto knew this well and said, "We shall receive a reward," and began searching. Because of this, many were discovered. Even among the low-born, those with fair skin and handsome features were summoned. When it was said, "This is the young master of the Chancellor's son, that one is the son of the Vice-Chancellor," although their parents wept in sorrow, saying, "That is the executioner's son, that one is the wet nurse's son," they were drowned, buried in the earth, crushed to death, or stabbed to death. There was no way to express the mother's grief or the wet nurse's lament. Even though the Hojo had many descendants and did not consider this particularly severe, since it was the custom of the times, they could not stop it.

text: 中にも小松三位中將殿若君、六代御前とておはす也、平家の嫡々なる上、年もおとなしうまします也。如何にもしてとり奉らんとて、手を分てもとめられけれども、求かねて下らんとせられける所に、或女房の六波羅に出て申けるは「是より西遍照寺の奧、大覺寺と申す山寺の北の方、菖蒲谷と申す所にこそ、小松三位中將殿の北方、若君、姫君おはしませ。」と申せば、時政やがて人をつけて其邊を窺はせける程に、或坊に女房達少き人餘たゆゝしく忍びたる體にて住ひけり。まがきの隙よりのぞきければ、白い狗の走出たるを取らんとて、美氣なる若君の出給へば、乳母の女房と覺しくて、「あな淺まし、人もこそ見參らすれ。」とて、いそぎ引入奉る。「是ぞ一定そにておはしますらん。」と思ひ、急ぎ走り歸てかくと申せば、次の日北條かしこに打向ひ、四方を打圍み、人をいれていはせけるは、「平家小松三位中將殿の若君六代御前、是におはしますと承はて、鎌倉殿の御代官に北條四郎時政と申者が、御迎に參て候、はや／＼出し參させ給へ。」と申されければ、母上之を聞給ふに、つや／＼物も覺え給はず。齋藤五、齋藤六、走り廻て見けれども、武士ども四方を打圍み、いづかたより出し奉るべしともおぼえず。乳母の女房も、御前に倒臥し、聲も惜まずをめき叫ぶ。日比は物をだにも高く云はず、忍つゝ隱れ居たりつれども、今は家の中にありとあるもの聲をとゝのへて泣悲しむ。北條も是を聞て世に心くるしげに思ひ、涙拭ひつく％＼とぞ待たれける。やゝ有て、重て申されけるは、「世もいまだしづまり候はねば、しどけなき事もぞ候とて御迎に參て候。別の御事は候まじ。はや／＼出し參らさせ給へ。」と申されければ、若君母上に申させ給ひけるは、「終に逃るまじう候へばとく／＼出させおはしませ。武士共うち入て、さがす物ならば、うたて氣なる御有樣共を見えさせ給ひなんず。たとひ罷出で候とも、暫しも候はゞ、暇乞て歸參り候はん。痛な歎かせ給ひそ。」と。慰め給ふこそいとほしけれ。

annotation.translation: Among them was the young Lord, the Third Rank Captain of Komatsu, who was known as the Sixth Generation of the Imperial Court; as the direct heir of the Taira clan, he was of mature age and possessed a noble character. Seeking to take him by force, they sent people to search for him, but he had resolved not to be found. At that time, a lady of the court went to Rokuhara and reported: 'To the west of this place, beyond the inner precincts of Hennenjo Temple, lies a mountain temple called Daikaku-ji, in the northern direction of Shobugaya; it is there that the young Lord, the Third Rank Captain of Komatsu, and the Princess, reside.' Upon hearing this, Tokimasa immediately sent people to spy on that area, and they found that in a certain hut, a few ladies-in-waiting had secretly taken up residence in a manner befitting their status. Peering through the gaps in the fence, they saw a white dog running out, and in an attempt to catch it, the beautiful young Lord came out. Mistaking him for a lady-in-waiting, one exclaimed, 'How unfortunate! Even a person has been seen.' They hurriedly brought him inside. Thinking, 'This is certainly where he is,' they rushed back and reported, 'He is here.' The next day, the Hojo clan marched toward that place, surrounded the area from all sides, and ordered their men to say: 'The Taira clan's young Lord, the Third Rank Captain of Komatsu, the Sixth Generation of the Imperial Court, is said to be here. Hojo Shiro Tokimasa, the governor of Kamakura, has come to receive him. Please send him out immediately.' Upon hearing this, his mother, though composed, could not speak. Saito Go and Saito Riku ran about searching, but the warriors surrounded them on all sides, and they could not discern from which direction they might escape. The lady-in-waiting, the wet nurse, fell at the young Lord's feet, crying out without holding back her tears. Until that day, they had not spoken loudly or openly, hiding quietly, but now, knowing they were inside the house, they began to wail and mourn together. The Hojo, hearing this, felt deep sorrow for the world, wiping away their tears in anticipation. After a while, they said again: 'Since the world has not yet settled, we have come to receive you, though it may seem improper. There is no other matter. Please send him out immediately.' The young Lord, upon hearing this, requested his mother: 'Since we cannot escape, let us go out at once. If the warriors come in to search, they will surely see the pitiful state of our household. Even if we must go out, if we are allowed to stay for a moment, we will ask for permission to return. Do not make us weep in pain.' Her heart was deeply moved by this comfort.

text: さても有るべきならねば、母上泣々御ぐし掻撫で物著せ奉り、既に出し奉らんとし給ひけるが、黒木の珠數のちいさう美しいを取出して、是にて如何にも成らんまで、念佛申て、極樂へ參れよ。」とて奉り給へば、わか君是を取て、「母御前には今日既に離れ參せなんず。今は如何にもして、父のおはしまさん所へぞ參りたき。」と宣ひけるこそ哀なれ。是を聞いて御妹の姫君の十に成り給ふが、「我も父御前の御許へまゐらん。」とて、走り出給ふを、乳母の女房とり留め奉る。六代御前、今年は僅に十二にこそ成り給へども尋常の十四五よりは長しく、みめかたち優におはしければ、「敵に弱げを見えじ。」とて、押ふる袖の隙よりも、餘て涙ぞこぼれける。さて御輿に乘り給ふ。武士共前後左右に打圍で出にけり。齋藤五、齋藤六、御輿の左右に附いてぞ參りける。北條乘替共下して、乘すれども乘らず、大覺寺より六波羅まで徒跣にてぞ走ける。母上乳母の女房、天に仰ぎ地に伏して悶え焦れ給ひけり。「此日來平家の子供取集めて、水に入るゝもあり、土に埋むもあり。押殺し、刺殺し、樣々にすと聞ゆれば、我子は、何としてか失はんずらん。少し長しければ、頸をこそ切んずらめ。人の子は乳母などの許に置きて、時々見る事も有り。それだにも恩愛の道は悲しき習ひぞかし。況や是は生落して後、一日片時も身をはなたず。人の持たぬ物を持ちたる樣に思ひて、朝夕二人の中にてそだてし者を、憑をかけし人にもあかで別し其後は、二人をうらうへにおきてこそ慰みつるに、一人はあれども一人はなし。今日より後は如何がせむ。此三年が間、夜晝肝心を消しつゝ思ひ設つる事なれども、さすが昨日今日とは思寄らず、年比長谷の觀音をこそ深う憑み奉りつるに、終にとられぬる事の悲しさよ。唯今もや失ひつらん。」と掻口説泣より外の事ぞなき。さ夜深けれども胸せきあぐる心ちして露もまどろみ給はぬが、良有て乳母の女房に宣ひけるは、「只今ちと打目睡みたりつる夢に、此子が白い馬に乘りて來つるが、『あまりに戀しう思參せ候へば暫し暇乞うて參りて候。』とて、傍につい居て、何とやらん世に恨しげに思ひてさめ％＼と泣きつるが、程なく打おどろかされて若やとかたはらを探れども人もなし。夢なりとも暫しもあらで、覺ぬる事の悲しさよ。」とぞ語り給ふ。乳母の女房も泣きけり。長き夜もいとど明しかねて涙に床も浮計なり。

annotation.translation: Then, if it were so, Mother wept bitterly, dressed him in fine robes and was about to take him out, but she took out a black wood bead that was small and beautiful, and said, 'Pray the Buddha until he becomes just like this, and go to the Pure Land.' She presented it, and the young lord took it and said, 'Today I must part with you, my dear Mother. Now I must do whatever is necessary and go to where my father is.' It was indeed pitiable. Hearing this, the Princess, his younger sister, who had just turned ten, said, 'I too shall go to my father's side,' and ran off, but the wet nurse and her attendant held her back. The Lady Roku, though this year she had only turned twelve, was taller than the usual fourteen or fifteen, and her appearance was exceedingly fine, so she said, 'I must not show weakness to the enemy.' Through the gap of the sleeve she was pushing, more tears flowed. Then she boarded the palanquin. The warriors surrounded her from all sides. Saito Go and Saito Roku followed on the left and right of the palanquin. The Hojo retainers dismounted and urged her to ride, but she did not ride; instead, from Daikaku-ji to Roku-hara, she ran on foot. Mother and the wet nurse looked up to heaven and prostrated themselves on the ground, writhing in anguish and despair. 'On this day, they have gathered the children of the Taira and either drowned them or buried them in the earth. They have been crushed, stabbed, and killed in various ways. I hear this, and I fear my child will be lost. Since he is a little older, they will surely cut his neck. Children of other people are left with their wet nurses, and one can visit them from time to time. That is also a sorrowful custom of love. How much more so when, after being born and raised, one is never parted from them even for a day or a moment? They have been raised as if they were a treasure beyond the reach of others, in the morning and evening, in the midst of the two of them. Even after the person who raised them has been taken away, the two of them have found solace in each other, but now there is one but not the other. What shall I do from today onward? For these three years, day and night, I have consumed my very soul in thought and worry, but I could not have foreseen that yesterday and today would come. I have deeply prayed to the Kannon of Hasedera for years, and now the sorrow of being taken away is unbearable. Could I have lost him even now?' She wept, her words turning into a torrent of tears. Though it was late at night, her heart was choked with grief, and even the dew seemed to sleep. Yoshinari said to the wet nurse, 'Just now, in a dream I briefly fell asleep, and this child came riding a white horse. He said, "Since I miss you so much, I shall take a short leave and come to you." He stood by my side, thinking, "What shall I do? I feel full of sorrow in this world," and then he woke up weeping. But shortly after, I was startled awake and searched for him on both sides, but there was no one. Even if it was a dream, the sorrow of waking up is unbearable.' He told this story. The wet nurse also wept. The long night could not end; the bed was soaked with tears.

text: 限あれば、鷄人曉を唱て夜もあけぬ。齋藤六歸り參りたり。「さて如何にやいかに。」と問ひ給へば「唯今までは別の御事も候はず。御文の候。」とて、取出いて奉る。あけて御覽ずれば「如何に御心苦しう思食され候らん。唯今までは別の事も候はず。いつしかたれ％＼も御戀しうこそ候へ。」とよに長しやかに書き給へり。母上是を見給ひて、とかうの事ものたまはず。御文をふどころに引入てうつぶしにぞなられける。誠に心の中さこそはおはしけめと推量られて哀なり。

annotation.translation: If there were a limit, the rooster would not crow at dawn and the night would not break. Saite returned and paid his respects. When he was asked, 'Now, what shall we do?', he replied, 'Until now, there has been no other matter; it is about your letter.' Then he took it out and presented it. When she opened and read it, it said, 'How greatly you must be troubled in your heart. Until now, there has been no other matter; before long, everyone will surely miss you.' It was written at length and in a sorrowful tone. The Empress, seeing this, did not speak of such things. She drew the letter into her lap and fell forward, prostrate. Truly, it must have been in her heart, and it was pitiable.

text: かくて遙に時刻推移りければ、齋藤六、「時の程も覺束なう候に、歸參らん。」と申せば、母上泣泣御返事書いて給でけり。齋藤六暇申て罷り出づ。乳母の女房責ても心のあられずさに、走り出でて何くを指ともなくその邊を足に任せて泣きありく程に、或人の申けるは、「此奧に高雄といふ山寺あり。その聖文覺坊と申人こそ、鎌倉殿にゆゝしき大事の人に思はれ參せておはしますが、上臈の御子を御弟子にせんとて、ほしがらるなれ。」と申ければ、嬉しき事を聞きぬと思ひて母上にかくとも申さず、唯一人高雄に尋入り、聖に向ひ奉て、「ちの中よりおほしたて參せて、今年十二に成らせ給ひつる若君を、昨日武士にとられて候。御命乞請參せ給ひて、御弟子にせさせ給ひなんや。」とて、聖の前に倒伏し、聲をも惜まず泣き叫ぶ。誠にせんかたなげにぞ見えたりける。聖無慚におぼえければ、事の仔細をとひ給ふ。起あがて泣々申けるは、「平家小松三位の中將の北方の親しうまします人の御子を養ひ奉るを、若中將殿の公達とや、人の申候ひけん。昨日武士の取り參せて罷り候ひぬるなり。」と申。「さて武士をば誰といひつる。」「北條とこそ申候ひつれ。」聖、「いでさらば行向ひて尋ねん。」とて、つき出ぬ。此詞を憑むべきにはあらねども、聖のかくいへば、今少し人の心ち出來て急ぎ大覺寺へ歸り參り、母上にかくと申せば、「身を投に出ぬるやらんと思ひて、我も如何ならん淵河にも身を投んと思ひたれば。」とて、事の仔細を問給ふ。聖の申つる樣を有のまゝに語りければ、「あはれ乞請て、今一度見せよかし。」とて、手を合せてぞ泣かれける。

annotation.translation: Thus, as time had passed long, Saitei Rokuro said, "The time of day is also indistinct; I shall return." Then, His Lady Mother, weeping, wrote a reply and sent it. Saitei Rokuro took his leave and departed. The wet nurse, unable to bear the distress in her heart, ran out and, with no destination in mind, wandered about the area letting her feet carry her, weeping. Then someone said, "There is a mountain temple called Takao in this region. That monk Shōmon Kaku-bō is held in high esteem by Lord Kamakura; indeed, he is thought to be a person of great importance to the Lord of Kamakura, and he is longing to make the young lady of the upper chamber his disciple." Hearing this joyful news, His Lady Mother did not tell anyone but went alone to seek out Takao. Facing the Saint, she said, "I beg you, by your grace, to have mercy upon the young lord, who has just turned twelve this year and was taken yesterday by a warrior. I pray you, plead for his life and make him your disciple." Then she prostrated herself before the Saint, weeping aloud without sparing her voice. Truly, she appeared utterly hopeless. Since the Saint felt no shame, he asked for the details of the matter. Rising up, weeping, she said, "The young son of the Northern Lady, the intimate of the Middle Counselor of the Taira family's Komatsu Third Rank, was reported by people as being the servant of Lord Wakunakagō. Yesterday, a warrior took him away and has now departed." "Then, who is this warrior?" "It is said to be Hōjō." The Saint said, "Then I shall go and inquire." And he set out. Although these words are not worthy of reliance, since the Saint said thus, I, with a slightly lightened heart, hastened to return to Daikaku-ji and told His Lady Mother. She said, "I thought you had thrown yourself into the water, so I too was about to throw myself into the same abyss." Then she asked for the details of the matter. Since I recounted the Saint's words exactly as they were, she said, "Truly, I beg you; let me see him once more." Then she clasped her hands and wept.

text: 聖六波羅に行むかて事の仔細を問ひ給ふ。北條申されけるは、「鎌倉殿の仰には、平家の子孫京中に多く忍んでありと聞く。中にも小松三位中將の子息中御門の新大納言の娘の腹にありと聞く。平家の嫡々なる上年もおとなしかんなり。如何にも尋出して、失ふべしと、仰を蒙て候ひしが、此程末々のをさなき人をば少々取奉て候つれども、此若君は在所をしり奉らず、尋かねて既に空しう罷下らんとし候つるが、思はざる外、一昨日聞出して、昨日迎へ奉て候へども、斜ならず美しうおはする間、あまりに最愛くて未ともかうもし奉らで置き參らせて候。」と申せば、聖、「いでさらば見奉らん。」とて、若君のおはしける處へ參て見參せ給へば、二重織物の直垂に、黒木の數珠手に貫入ておはします。髮のかゝり姿骨柄誠にあてに美しく此世の人とも見え給はず。今夜打とけて、寢給はぬと覺しくて、少し面痩給へるにつけていとゞ心苦しうらうたくぞ覺えける。聖を御覽じて、何とかおぼしけん。涙ぐみ給へば、聖も是を見奉てそゞろに墨染の袖をぞ絞りける。縱ひ末の世に如何なるあた敵になるとも、いかゞ是を失ひ奉るべきと悲しうおぼえければ、北條に宣ひけるは、「此若君を見奉るに、先世の事にや候らん、餘りに最愛う思ひ奉り候。廿日が命を延べて給べ。鎌倉殿へ參て申預り候はむ。聖鎌倉殿を世にあらせ奉らんとて我身も流人でありながら院宣伺ひ奉らんとて京へ上るに、案内も知らぬ富士川の尻に夜渡り懸て、既に押流されんとしたりし事、高市の山にてひはぎにあひ、手をすて命ばかり生、福原の籠の御所へ參り、前右兵衞督光能卿に付き奉て院宣申出て奉りし時の御約束には、如何なる大事をも申せ、聖が申さん事をば、頼朝が一期の間は叶へんとこそ宣ひしか。其後も度々の奉公かつは見給ひし事なれば、事新う始めて申べきにあらず、契を重うし命を輕うす。鎌倉殿に受領神つき給はずば、よも忘れ給はじ。」とて、其曉立にけり。齋藤五、齋藤六、是をきゝ聖を生身の佛の如く思ひて、手を合て涙を流す。急ぎ大覺寺へ參て、この由申ければ、是を聞き給ひける母上の心の中いかばかりかは嬉かりけん。されども鎌倉のはからひなれば、いかゞあらんずらむと覺束なけれども、當時聖の憑し氣に申て下ぬる上、廿日の命の延給に、母上乳母の女房少し心も取延て、偏に觀音の御助なればと憑しうぞ思はれける。

annotation.translation: The Saint went to the Sacred Roka and asked about the details of the matter. Hojo replied, "I have heard that among the descendants of the Taira, many are hiding in the capital, and specifically, it is said that the daughter of the new Dainagon Shomimon, by the womb of the son of Shomimon Sanmi, is among them. The legitimate heir of the Taira is indeed quite mature. I was commanded to search thoroughly and eliminate him. Recently, I have taken in a few insignificant people, but this young lord, not knowing his own place, had already come back empty-handed without being found. Unexpectedly, I learned of him the day before yesterday, and brought him in yesterday. However, since he is not only handsome but also extremely beautiful, and I could not bear to harm him, I have left him here as he is." Upon hearing this, the Saint said, "Very well, I shall go and see him." He went to where the young lord was and looked upon him. He was wearing a black silk chrysanthemum-patterned robe, with a black wooden rosary held in his hand. His hair was styled in a manner most beautiful, and his figure was so graceful that he did not seem like a man of this world. Tonight, he stayed awake and did not sleep, and his face appeared somewhat thin, which made me feel all the more sorrowful and distressed. When he saw the Saint, he seemed to think of something. As tears welled in his eyes, the Saint, seeing this, also squeezed the sleeves of his ink-dyed kimono in unison. Even if in the end he were to become an enemy of the world, how could I bear to lose him? He mourned deeply and said to Hojo, "When I see this young lord, I feel as though it were a matter of the past life; I love him so much. Please extend his life for twenty days. I shall go to Kamakura and make a request to the Lord of Kamakura. The Saint, wishing to establish the Lord of Kamakura in the world, although I myself am an exile, went to the capital to seek the Imperial Decree. At night, I crossed the lower reaches of the Fuji River, where I had no guide, and was nearly swept away by the current. On the mountain of Takaki, I met Hiba, abandoned my hand, and barely survived. I went to the Palace of the Fuku no Kago, and when I presented the Imperial Decree with the support of Mitsuhiro, the former Right General of the Guard, the agreement was that whatever important matter I would request, the Lord of Kamakura would grant it during his lifetime. Since I have served him repeatedly and he has seen my loyalty, there is no need to start anew. The covenant is heavy, and life is light. If the Lord of Kamakura does not accept the divine decree, he will surely not forget." With these words, he rose at dawn. Saito Go and Saito Roku, hearing this, regarded the Saint as if he were a living Buddha, joined their hands, and shed tears. They hurriedly went to Daikaku-ji Temple and reported the matter. How joyful the heart of his mother, who heard this, must have been! However, since it was the plan of Kamakura, he felt uneasy, wondering what could be done. Nevertheless, the Saint had previously spoken in a state of divine possession, and with the extension of the twenty-day life, his mother and the nursemaids of the lady felt somewhat relieved, thinking that it was undoubtedly the help of the Goddess Kannon.

I went to the Palace of the Fuku no Kago, and when I presented the Imperial Decree with the support of Mitsuhiro, the former Right General of the Guard, the agreement was that whatever important matter I would request, the Lord of Kamakura would grant it during his lifetime. Since I have served him repeatedly and he has seen my loyalty, there is no need to start anew. The covenant is heavy, and life is light. If the Lord of Kamakura does not accept the divine decree, he will surely not forget." With these words, he rose at dawn. Saito Go and Saito Roku, hearing this, regarded the Saint as if he were a living Buddha, joined their hands, and shed tears. They hurriedly went to Daikaku-ji Temple and reported the matter. How joyful the heart of his mother, who heard this, must have been! However, since it was the plan of Kamakura, he felt uneasy, wondering what could be done. Nevertheless, the Saint had previously spoken in a state of divine possession, and with the extension of the twenty-day life, his mother and the nursemaids of the lady felt somewhat relieved, thinking that it was undoubtedly the help of the Goddess Kannon.

text: かくてあかし暮し給ふ程に、廿日の過るは夢なれや。聖はいまだ見えざりけり、何と成ぬる事やらんとなか／＼心苦うて、今更又悶え焦れ給ひけり。北條も、「文覺房の約束の日數もすぎぬ、さのみ在京して、年を暮すべきにもあらず。今は下らん。」とてひしめきければ、齋藤五、齋藤六、手を握り肝魂を碎けども、聖も未だ見え給はず、使者をだにも上せねば、思ふばかりぞ無りける。此等大覺寺へ歸り參て、「聖も未だ上り給はず、北條も曉下向仕候。」とて、左右の袖を顏に押當て涙をはらはらと流す。是を聞き給ひける母上の心の中如何ばかりかは悲しかりけむ。「哀長しやかならん者の聖の行逢ん所まで六代を具せよと言へかし。若乞請ても上らんに先に斬りたらん悲しさをば如何せむずる。さてとく失ひげなるか。」と宣へば、「やがて此曉の程とこそ見えさせ給候へ。其故は、此程御とのゐ仕候つる北條の家子郎等ども、よに名殘惜氣に思ひ參せて或は念佛申す者も候。或は涙を流す者も候。」「さて此子は何として有ぞ。」と宣へば、「人の見まゐらせ候時は、さらぬ樣にもてないて、御數珠をくらせおはしまし候が、人の候はぬ時は、御袖を御顏に押當て、涙に咽ばせ給ひ候。」と申。「さこそあるらめ。をさなけれども、心長しやかなる者なり。今夜限りの命と思て、いかに心細かるらん。暫しもあらば、いとま乞て參らんといひしかども、廿日にあまるに、あれへも行かず、是へも見えず。今日より後又何れの日何れの時相見るべしともおぼえず。さて汝等は如何が計らふ」と宣へば、「是はいづくまでも御供仕り、むなしう成せ給ひて候はゞ御骨を取り奉り高野の御山に納奉り、出家入道して後世を弔ひまゐらせんとこそ思ひなて候へ。」と申。「さらば餘りに覺束なう覺ゆるに、とう歸れ。」と宣へば、二人の者泣々暇申て罷出づ。さる程に、同十二月十六日北條四郎若君具し奉て既に都を立にけり。齋藤五、齋藤六、涙にくれて行先も見えねども、最後の所までと思ひつゝ泣々御供に參りけり。北條、「馬に乘れ。」と云へども乘らず。「最後の供で候へば、苦しう候まじ。」とて、血の涙を流しつつ脚にまかせてぞ下ける。六代御前はさしも離れ難くおぼしける母上乳母の女房にも別果て、住馴し都をも雲井の餘所に顧みて、今日を限の東路におもむかれけん心の中、推量られて哀なり。駒を早むる武士あれば、我頸討んずるかと肝をけし、物言ひかはす人あれば、既に今やと心を盡す。四宮河原と思へ共、關山をも打越えて、大津の浦に成にけり。粟津が原かと窺へども今日もはや暮にけり。國々宿々打過々々行程に、駿河國にもつき給ひぬ。若君の露の御命、今日を限とぞ聞えける。

annotation.translation: Thus, as His Holiness was spending his days in such a manner, had the twentieth day passed as in a dream? His Holiness had not yet appeared; what had become of him, and why was he so distressed and troubled in his heart? The Hōjō also said, "The number of days agreed upon by the monk Bunkaku has already passed; there is no need for him to remain so long in the capital and spend the year-end here. Let him descend now." Upon this, they pressed forward, and even though Saitō Go and Saitō Six held hands and broke their very souls, His Holiness still did not appear, and no messenger had even been sent upward, so they were left with nothing but their thoughts. Returning to this Daikaku-ji, they reported, "His Holiness has not yet ascended, and the Hōjō has already departed for the lower regions," and they pressed their sleeves to their faces, letting tears fall in great drops. Upon hearing this, how sorrowful must have been the heart of his noble mother! "Say that the long-suffering His Holiness is to be brought to the place where the six generations will be completed. If even if he is begged for, he will not ascend, how can we deal with the sorrow of cutting him down beforehand? Alas, he is lost so quickly!" When he declared thus, they said, "It is only now, at this early hour, that it has become clear. The reason is that the young retainers of the Hōjō house, who have been serving His Holiness lately, are deeply reluctant to part, and some are chanting the Buddha's name, while others are shedding tears." "Then what is the purpose of this child?" he asked. "When people are present, he does not behave in any special way, but wears the rosary and sits in meditation; however, when no one is present, he presses his sleeves to his face and chokes on his tears." "That must be so. Though still young, he is a person of deep feelings. Thinking that tonight is the limit of his life, how distressed he must be. If there were even a moment's delay, he would have begged for leave and departed, but now, having passed the twentieth day, he has not gone to that place, nor has he appeared here. From today onward, I cannot imagine when or on what day we shall meet again. How, then, do you propose to act?" When he asked thus, they replied, "We will accompany you wherever you go. If you should pass away in vain, we will collect your bones and enshrine them on Mount Koya, become monks, and offer prayers for your salvation in the next world." "Then, since you are so bewildered and uncertain, go back now." When he declared thus, the two men, weeping, took their leave and departed. At that time, on the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, the young lord Hōjō Shiro, having gathered his entourage, had already left the capital. Saitō Go and Saitō Six, weeping so that they could not see the road ahead, thinking that this was the final moment, accompanied him weeping. Even though the Hōjō said, "Mount your horses," they did not. "Since this is the last journey, we shall not suffer hardship," they said, and, shedding blood-tears, they let their legs carry them downward. Even though the Sixth Emperor had found it so difficult to part from his mother, the lady-in-waiting who had nursed him, he turned his gaze from the capital he had grown accustomed to, as if looking at clouds in the sky, and set out on the eastern road, limiting his journey to today; the sorrow in his heart was beyond measure. Seeing warriors hastening their steeds, he feared they might strike at his neck, and his heart was shaken; when people spoke to him, he felt his spirit was already exhausted. Even though they thought they had reached the Yashima River Plain, they crossed over the Sekiyama Mountains and arrived at Ōtsu no Ura. Even though they wondered if it was Awazu no Hara, today had already drawn to dusk. Traveling through various provinces and inns, they reached Suruga Province. It was heard that the dew-like life of the young lord was limited to this day.

text:
千本の松原に武士共皆下り居て御輿舁居させ、敷皮敷いて若君を居奉る。北條四郎若君の御前近う參て申されけるは、「是まで具し參せ候つるは別の事候はず。若道にて聖にもや行逢ひ候、と待ち過し參せ候つる也。御心ざしの程は見えまゐらせ候ぬ。山のあなたまでは、鎌倉殿の御心中をも知りがたう候へば、近江國にて失ひ參せて候由披露仕候べし。誰申候共、一業所感の御事なれば、よも叶はじ。」と泣々申ければ、
若君ともかうも其返事をばし給はず。齋藤五、齋藤六をちかう召て、「我如何にも成りなん後、汝等都に歸て、穴賢、道にてきられたりとは申すべからず。其故は、終には隱れあるまじけれども、正しう此有樣聞いて、餘に歎き給はゞ、草の影にても心苦しうおぼえて後世の障りともならんずるぞ。鎌倉まで送りつけて參て候と申べし。」と宣へば、二人の者共肝魂も銷果て暫しは御返事にも及ばず。稍有て齋藤五「君におくれまゐらせて後命生て安穩に都まで上りつくべしとも覺候はず。」と涙を抑てふしにけり。既に今はの時に成しかば、若君御ぐしの肩にかゝりたりけるを、よにうつくしき御手をもて前へ打越し給ひたりければ、守護の武士ども見まゐらせて「あないとほし。いまだ御心のましますよ。」とて皆袖をぞぬらしける。其後西にむかひ手を合て靜に念佛唱つゝ頸をのべてぞ待給ふ。狩野工藤三親俊切手にえらばれ、太刀を引側めて左の方より御後に立廻り、既に切り奉らんとしけるが、目も暮れ心も消果て、何くに太刀を打つくべしとも覺えず、前後不覺に成りしかば、「仕つとも覺候はず、他人に仰附られ候へ。」とて、太刀を捨て退にけり。「さらば、あれ切れ、これ切れ。」とて、切手を選ぶ處に、墨染の衣著て月毛なる馬に乘たる僧一人、鞭をあげてぞ馳たりける。「あないとほし、あの松原の中に、世にうつくしき若君を、北條殿の斬らせたまふぞや。」とて、者どもひし／＼と走り集りければ、此僧「あな心う」とて、手をあがいてまねきけるが、猶おぼつかなさに、きたる笠をぬぎ、指上てぞ招ける。北條「仔細あり。」とて待處に此僧走ついて、急ぎ馬より飛おり、暫く息を休めて、「若君許されさせ給ひて候。鎌倉殿の御教書是に候。」とて取出して奉る。北條披て見給へば、誠や、
北條四郎殿へ　　　　頼朝

After reading it back and forth a few times, it said, 'Truly divine, truly divine,' and since it was set aside, there was no need for Saito Go and Saito Roku to speak; even the Hōjō family's retainers all shed tears of joy.

text:
さる程に、文覺房もつと出きたり、若君乞請たりとて、氣色誠にゆゆしげなり。
「『此若君の父三位中將殿は、初度の戰の大將軍也。誰申とも叶ふまじ。』と宣ひつ
れば『文覺が心を破ては、爭か冥加もおはすべき。』など惡口申つれども、猶『叶ま
じ。』とて、那須野の狩に下り給し間、剩文覺も狩場の供して、漸々に申てこひ請た
り。いかに遲うおぼしつらん。」と申されければ、北條「廿日と仰せられ候ひし御約
束の日數も過候ぬ。鎌倉殿の御宥れなきよと存じて、具し奉て下る程に、かしこうぞ、
爰にて誤ち仕候らんに。」とて、鞍置て引せたる馬共に齋藤五、齋藤六を乘せて上せ
らる。我身も遙に打送り奉て、「暫く御供申たう候へども、鎌倉殿に指て申べき大事
共候。暇申て。」とて打別れてぞ下られける。誠に情深かりけり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, Honenbō came out more and more, saying that the young lord had requested it, and his demeanor was truly ominous. "The young lord's father, the Daisan Shōshō, was the Great General in the first battle. No one, whoever they may be, can grant this," he declared. Yet, "If you break Honenbō's heart, how could any favor be granted?" and so on, he spoke ill of him, but still, "It cannot be done," he said. When he descended for the hunt at Nasuno, Honenbō, too, joined the hunt party and gradually pleaded earnestly. "How long will you delay?" he was told. The Hōjō replied, "The agreed number of days you promised, twenty days, has not yet passed. I fear there will be no pardon from the Lord of Kamakura. Therefore, as I am preparing to descend, how unfortunate it is that I should make a mistake here." With that, he placed a saddle on his horse and mounted it with Saitō Go and Saitō Roku. Even I, being sent off from afar, said, "Although I shall accompany you for a while, there are important matters to report to the Lord of Kamakura. I must take my leave." Thus we parted ways and descended. Truly, it was a display of deep affection.

text: 聖若君を請とり奉て、夜を日についで馳上る程に、尾張國熱田の邊にて、今年も既に暮ぬ。明る正月五日の夜に入て、都へ上り著く。二條猪熊なる所に、文覺坊の宿房ありければ、其に入奉て、暫く休奉り、夜半ばかり大覺寺へぞおはしける。門をたゝけども、人なければ音もせず。築地の壞より若君の飼ひ給ひける白い狗の走り出て、尾を振て向ひけるに、若君「母上はいづくに在ますぞ。」ととはれけるこそせめての事なれ。齋藤六、築地を越え、門を開て入奉る。近う人の住だる所とも見えず。若君「いかにもしてかひなき命をいかばやと思しも戀しき人を今一度見ばやと思ふ爲なり。こはされば何と成り給ひけるぞや。」とて夜もすがら泣悲み給ふぞ誠に理と覺えて哀なる。夜を待明して近里の者に尋給へば、「年の内は大佛參りとこそ承候ひしか。正月の程は、長谷寺に御籠と聞え候しが、其後は御宿所へ人の通ふとも見え給はず。」と申ければ、齋藤五急ぎ長谷へ參て尋あひ奉り、此由申ければ、母上、乳母の女房つや／＼現とも覺え給はず、「是はされば夢かや夢か。」とぞ宣ひける。急ぎ大覺寺へ出させたまひ、若君を御覽じて嬉しさにも只先立つ物は涙なり。「疾々出家し給へ。」と仰られけれども、聖惜み奉て、出家もせさせ奉らず。やがて迎へとて高雄に置奉り、北の方の幽なる御有樣をも訪ひけるとこそ聞えし。觀音の大慈大悲は、罪有も罪無をも助給へば昔もかゝるためし多しといへども、ありがたかりし事共なり。

annotation.translation: Having requested Saint Waka no Kimi and having him conveyed, while racing on through the night and day, when they arrived at the outskirts of Atsuta in Owari Province, the year had already ended. Entering the night of the fifth day of the bright New Year, they ascended to the capital and arrived. Since there was a lodging of Monk Monjaku at a place called Niyo Inokuma, they entered it, rested for a while, and around midnight proceeded to Daikaku-ji. They knocked on the gate, but since there was no one, no sound came forth. A white dog that the young prince had raised ran out from the breach in the earthen wall, wagged its tail, and faced them. The young prince, having cried out, "Where is my mother?" was indeed the only thing that could be done. Saito Rokuro crossed the wall, opened the gate, and entered. There did not appear to be any place where people lived. The young prince said, "It is truly that I have thought to do whatever I can with this worthless life, and because I wish to see the person I love once more. What has become of you, given this?" and throughout the night he wept bitterly, which truly seemed reasonable and sorrowful. Waiting until dawn, he asked the people of the nearby village, "I heard that within the year you made a pilgrimage to the Great Buddha. During the New Year, it was heard that you went into seclusion at Hasedera, but after that, no one has been seen going to your residence." When he was told this, Saito Go hurried to Hasedera, went to inquire, and reported this. The mother, even the wet nurse and the female attendant Tsuya, did not appear to be there at all. "If so, is this a dream, is this a dream?" she exclaimed. He quickly had them dispatched to Daikaku-ji, where the young prince was viewed, and in his joy, only tears came forth before anything else. Although he was commanded, "Quickly take the tonsure," Saint Waka, out of pity, did not even allow him to take the tonsure. Soon, they set him to be received, placed him in Takao, and it is heard that they also visited the secluded residence of the northern lady. The Great Compassion and Great Mercy of the Bodhisattva Kannon, which has aided both those with sin and those without, has many such examples in the past, yet these are indeed remarkable events.

"If so, is this a dream, is this a dream?" she exclaimed. He quickly had them dispatched to Daikaku-ji, where the young prince was viewed, and in his joy, only tears came forth before anything else. Although he was commanded, "Quickly take the tonsure," Saint Waka, out of pity, did not even allow him to take the tonsure. Soon, they set him to be received, placed him in Takao, and it is heard that they also visited the secluded residence of the northern lady. The Great Compassion and Great Mercy of the Bodhisattva Kannon, which has aided both those with sin and those without, has many such examples in the past, yet these are indeed remarkable events.

text: さる程に北條四郎六代御前具し奉て下りけるに、鎌倉殿御使鏡宿にて行合たりけるに、「如何に」と問へば、「十郎藏人殿、信太三郎先生殿、九郎判官殿に同心の由聞え候。討奉れとの御氣色で候。」と申。北條「吾身は大事の召人具したれば。」とて甥の北條平六時貞が送りに下りけるを、おいその森より「疾和殿は歸て此人人おはし處聞出して討て參せよ。」とてとゞめらる。平六都に歸て尋る程に十郎藏人殿の在所知たりといふ法師出來たり。彼僧に尋れば「我はくはしうはしらず、知りたりといふ僧こそあれ。」といひければ、押寄せて彼僧を搦捕る。「是はなんの故に搦るぞ」。「十郎藏人殿の在所知たなれば搦むる也。」「さらば教へよとこそいはめ。さうなうからむる事は如何に。天王寺にとこそ聞け。」「さらばじんじよせよ。」とて、平六が聟の小笠原十郎國久、殖原九郎、桑原次郎、服部平六を先として其勢三十餘騎、天王寺へ發向す。十郎藏人の宿は二所あり。谷の學頭伶人兼春秦六秦七と云者の許也。二手に作て押寄たり。十郎藏人は兼春が許におはしけるが、物具したる者共の打入を見て後より落にけり。學頭が娘二人あり。ともに藏人のおもひものなり。是等を捕へて藏人のゆくへを尋ぬれば姉は「妹に問へ。」といふ。妹は「姉に問へ。」といふ。俄に落ぬる事なれば、誰にもよも知らせじなれども、具して京へぞ上りける。

annotation.translation: As the Hōjō Shiro Rokudai prepared his gear and descended, he happened to meet the Kamakura Lord's messenger at the Kagami Inn. When asked, 'How is it?', the messenger replied, 'Lord Jūrō Kurōdono and Lord Shinta Saburō Sensei, and Lord Kyūrō Kannon, have joined forces; it is reported that they intend to attack.' Hearing this, Hōjō said, 'I have mustered men for a major mission.' Yet, as his nephew Hōjō Hira Rokutoki Tokisada was escorting him down, from the nearby Mori Forest, a voice called out, 'Haya no Wa, return at once, find out where this man is, and kill him.' Tokisada was detained. Returning to the main path and inquiring further, a monk appeared who claimed to know the whereabouts of Lord Jūrō Kurō. When questioned by Tokisada, the monk replied, 'I do not know; I am merely a monk who claims to know.' Pressing him, they captured the monk. 'Why are you capturing me?' the monk asked. 'Because you claim to know the whereabouts of Lord Jūrō Kurō,' they answered. 'Then tell us,' the monk urged. 'How can you be so certain? I heard he is at Tennoji Temple.' 'Then summon help,' they said. Thus, Hira Rokutoki's son-in-law, Ogisawara Jūrō Kunihisa, along with Uehara Kyūrō, Kuwahara Jirō, and Hattori Hira Rokutoki, led a force of over thirty riders and set out for Tennoji Temple. Lord Jūrō Kurō had two residences: one at the house of Tani no Gakudō, the actor Kenjin, and another at the house of Bishin Rokudai and Bishin Nanadai. They attacked from two directions. Lord Jūrō Kurō was at Kenjin's residence, but upon seeing the attackers, he fled from behind. The Gakudō had two daughters, both of whom were Lord Kurō's concubines. Capturing them and questioning them for Kurō's whereabouts, the elder sister said, 'Ask my younger sister.' The younger sister replied, 'Ask my elder sister.' Though it was sudden and he could not tell anyone, he nonetheless prepared his gear and ascended to Kyoto.

text: 藏人は熊野の方へ落けるが、只一人ついたりける侍、足を疾ければ、和泉國八木郷といふ處に逗留してこそ居たりけれ。彼の主の男、藏人を見知て夜もすがら京へ馳上り、北條平六につげたりければ「天王寺の手の者はいまだのぼらず、誰をか遣るべき。」とて大源次宗春といふ郎等をようで「汝が宮立たりし山僧はいまだあるか。」「さ候。」「さらば呼べ。」とて、喚ばれければ、件の法師出來たり。「十郎藏人のまします。討て鎌倉殿に參せて御恩蒙り給へ。」と云ければ、「承り候ぬ。人を給び候へ。」と申。「軈て大源次下れ、人もなきに。」とて舍人雜色人數僅に十四五人相そへてつかはす。常陸房正明と云者也。和泉國に下つき彼家に走り入て見れ共なし。板敷打破てさがし、塗ごめの内を見れ共なし。常陸房大路に立て見れば、百姓の妻とおぼしくて長敷き女の通りけるを捕へて、「此邊に恠しばうたる旅人のとどまたる處やある。いはずば切て捨ん。」と云へば、「只今さがされ候つる家にこそ夜邊まで世に尋常なる旅人の二人とどまて候つるが、今朝など出て候ふやらん。あれに見え候ふ大屋にこそ今は候ふなれ。」と云ひければ、常陸房黒革威の腹卷の袖著けたるに大太刀帶て彼家に走入てみれば、歳五十計なる男のかちの直垂に折烏帽子著て唐瓶子菓子などとりさばくり、銚子どももて酒勸めむとする處に、物具したる法師の打入を見て、かいふいて逃ければやがて續いて逐懸たり。藏人「あの僧。や、それは在ぬぞ。行家はこゝにあり。」と宣へば、走歸て見るに白い小袖に大口ばかり著て、左の手には金作りの小太刀をもち、右の手には野太刀の大なるを持たれたり。常陸房「太刀投させ給へ。」と申せば、藏人大に笑はれけり。常陸房走寄てむずと切る。丁と合せて跳り退く。又寄て切る。丁と合せてをどりのく。寄合寄逃き一時ばかりぞ戰うたる。藏人後なる塗籠の内へしざり入らんとし給へば、常陸房「まさなう候。な入せ給ひ候そ。」と申せば、「行家もさこそ思へ。」とて又跳り出て戰ふ。常陸房太刀を棄てむずと組んでどうと臥す。上に成り下に成り、ころび合ふ處に、大源次つと出きたり。餘に遽てゝ帶たる太刀をば拔で、石を握て藏人の額をはたと打て打破る。藏人大に笑て「己は下臈なれば。太刀長刀でこそ敵をばうて。礫にて敵打樣やある。」常陸房「足を結へ。」とぞ下知しける。常陸房は敵が足を結へとこそ申けるに、餘に遽てて四の足をぞ結たりける。其後藏人の頸に繩を懸て搦め引起して押居たり。「水參せよ。」と宣へば干飯を洗て參せたり。水をばめして、干飯をばめさず差し置き給へば、常陸房取て食うてけり。「和僧は山法師か。」「山法師で候。」「誰といふぞ。」西塔の北谷法師常陸房正明と申者で候。」「さては行家に仕はれむといひし僧か。」「さ候。」「頼朝が使か。平六が使歟。」「鎌倉殿の御使候。誠に鎌倉殿をば討參せんと思めし候ひしか。」「是程の身に成て後思はざりしといはゞ如何に、思ひしといはば如何に。手次の程はいかゞ思程の身に成て後思はざりしといはゞ如何に、思ひしといはば如何に。手次の程はいかゞ思ひつる。」と宣へば、「山上にて多の事に逢て候に、未だ是程手剛き事に合候はず、よき敵三人に逢たる心地こそし候つれ。」と申す。「さて正明をばいかゞ思召され候つる。」と申せば、「それはとられなん上は。」とぞ宣ひける。「其太刀取寄せよ。」とて見給へば、藏人の太刀は一所も不切常陸房が太刀は四十二所切れたりけり。やがて傳馬立させ乘奉て上るほどに、其夜は江口の長者が許に泊て夜もすがら使を走らかす。明る日の午刻ばかり北條平六其勢百騎ばかり旗さゝせて下るほどに淀の赤井河原で行合たり。「都へはいれ奉るべからずといふ院宣で候。鎌倉殿の御氣色も其儀でこそ候へ。はや／＼御頸を給はて鎌倉殿の見參にいれて御恩蒙り給へ。」といへば、さらばとて赤井河原で十郎藏人の頸を切る。

annotation.translation: The attendant was fleeing toward Kumano, but only one samurai managed to catch up with him; because his horse was swift, he stopped and stayed in a place called Yagi-gō in Izumi Province. The man's lord, seeing the attendant, raced all night to Kyoto and reported to Hōjō Heiroku, saying, "The men from Tennoji have not yet ascended; whom should we send?" He then dispatched a young retainer named Ōgenji Mochiharu, saying, "Is the mountain monk who was with your lord still there?" "He is," came the reply. "Then summon him." When summoned, the monk in question appeared. "The tenth attendant is present. Strike him down and present his head to the Lord of Kamakura so that you may receive a reward." "I have heard," the monk replied, "but do not order me to kill a man." "Then Ōgenji, come down! There are no others." He ordered that only a small retinue of about fourteen or fifteen men, including attendants and foot soldiers, accompany him. This man was Hitachi-bō Shōmyō. He descended to Izumi Province, ran to that house, and searched thoroughly, but found nothing. He broke open the floorboards and searched inside the lacquered chamber, but found nothing. Standing on Hitachi-bō's road, he spotted a woman who looked like a farmer's wife walking with a long skirt and captured her, saying, "Is there any place nearby where a strange traveler might have stayed? Speak, or I will cut you down and discard you." "Just now, they searched the house where two ordinary travelers of the world had stayed until nightfall, but this morning they likely went out. They are now at that large house you can see over there," she replied. Upon hearing this, Hitachi-bō, wearing a black-lacquered armor with sleeves and a large sword at his waist, rushed into that house. There he found a man of about fifty years, dressed in a direct-style garment with a folded black hat, scattering things like a Chinese bottle and sweets, and preparing to offer sake with a cup. Seeing the monk who had entered, the man fled in panic, and Hitachi-bō immediately pursued him. The attendant shouted, "That monk! No, that one is not here. My master is here." Running back to look, they saw him wearing a white undershirt with a wide collar, holding a small golden sword in his left hand and a large wild sword in his right. Hitachi-bō said, "Throw your sword down!" The attendant laughed loudly. Hitachi-bō ran forward and struck with a sudden slash. The attendant dodged with a leap. Hitachi-bō attacked again. The attendant dodged with a leap again. They clashed, retreated, and fought for a brief moment. When the attendant attempted to retreat into the lacquered chamber behind, Hitachi-bō said, "No, do not enter!" The attendant replied, "My master also thought so," and leaped out again to fight. Hitachi-bō dropped his sword, grappled fiercely, and threw the attendant to the ground. As they rolled and struggled, Ōgenji suddenly appeared. In his haste, he drew his sword, grabbed a stone, and struck the attendant's forehead, shattering it. The attendant laughed loudly, saying, "Since I am a lowly servant, I should have fought with a long sword or a large sword. What use is a stone to strike an enemy?" Hitachi-bō ordered, "Bind his legs." Hitachi-bō had ordered him to bind the enemy's legs, but in his haste, he bound the attendant's four legs. Afterward, they tied a rope around the attendant's neck, strangled him, and held him down. "Give me water," the attendant commanded. They washed the dry rice and offered it to him. However, they did not drink the water nor eat the dry rice themselves, leaving them for Hitachi-bō to take and eat. "Are you a mountain monk?" "I am a mountain monk." "Who are you?" "I am the monk from the Northern Valley of Sai-tō, Hitachi-bō Shōmyō." "So you are the monk who claimed to serve the master?" "Yes." "Did Yoritomo send you, or Heiroku?" "I am the messenger of the Lord of Kamakura. Did you truly intend to kill the Lord of Kamakura?" "If I say I did not think so after reaching this state, what then? If I say I did think so, what then? How did you plan it?" he asked. The monk replied, "I have encountered many things on the mountain, but I have never yet faced such a fierce opponent as this. I feel as though I have met three excellent foes." "Then, what do you think of Shōmyō?" he asked. "He will be captured, that is all," the monk replied. "Bring that sword here," he ordered. Upon inspection, the attendant's sword was not even slightly damaged, while Hitachi-bō's sword had forty-two notches. They immediately set up a relay horse, mounted him, and began their ascent. That night, they stayed at the residence of the wealthy man at Eguchi and sent messengers running all night. By noon the next day, Hōjō Heiroku, with a force of about one hundred horsemen and flags raised, descended and met them at the Akai River Plain in Yodo. "It is forbidden to enter the capital due to an imperial decree," he said. "The Lord of Kamakura's mood is also like this. Quickly, offer your neck so that the Lord of Kamakura may see it and you may receive a reward." So, at the Akai River Plain, they cut off the tenth attendant's neck.

text: 信太三郎先生義教は醍醐の山に籠たる由聞しかば、おし寄てさがせどもなし。伊賀の方へ落ぬと聞えしかば、服部平六を先として伊賀國へ發向す。千度の山寺にありと聞えし間、押寄てからめんとするに袷の小袖に大口ばかり著て金にて打くゝんだる腰の刀にて腹掻切てぞ伏たりける。頸をば服部平六とてけり。やがて持せて京へ上り、北條平六に見せたりければ「やがて持せて下り、鎌倉殿の見參に入て御恩蒙給へ。」といひければ常陸房服部各頸共持せて鎌倉へ下り見參に入たりければ、「神妙なり。」とて常陸房は笠井へ流さる。「下りはては勸賞蒙らんとこそ思ひつるに、さこそ無らめ、剩流罪に處せらるゝ條存外の次第也。かかるべしと知りたらば、何しか身命を捨けん。」と後悔すれども甲斐ぞなき。されども中二年といふに召返され「大將軍討たる者は冥加のなければ一旦戒めつるぞ。」とて但馬國に多田庄、攝津國に葉室二箇所給はて歸り上る。服部平六平家の祗候の人たりしかば沒官せられたりける服部かへし給はてけり。

annotation.translation: When we heard that Shinta no Saburō, the teacher Yoshinori, was shut up on the mountain at Daigo, we went forward to search for him, but found nothing. When we heard that he had fled toward Iga, we set out for Iga Province with Hattori Heiroku leading. While we heard he was at the Thousand-Temple Mountain, we advanced to engage him; he was wearing a thin kimono over his lower garment, a wide collar, and with a sword at his waist, he cut his own belly and fell down. His head was taken by Hattori Heiroku. Soon they carried it up to Kyoto and showed it to Hōjō Heiroku, who said, "Carry it down immediately and present it to the Lord of Kamakura to receive his reward." When they carried both heads down to Kamakura and presented them, he said, "It is divine and wondrous." However, Hitachi-bō Hattori was exiled to Kasai. "I had thought to receive a reward for bringing him down, but now I am to be punished for an extra crime beyond measure. If I had known this would happen, how could I have thrown away my life?" he regretted, but it was in vain. Nevertheless, because he had served for two years, he was summoned back: "Those who have attacked the Great General have no merit; once they have been warned, that is enough." So he was given two estates: one in Tajima Province, the other in Settsu Province, and he returned to the capital. Since Hattori Heiroku had been an attendant of the Taira clan, his confiscated estate was returned to him.

text:
さる程に、六代御前はやう／＼、十四五にも成給へば、みめ容いよ／＼うつくしく、あたりも照り輝くばかりなり。母上是を御覽じて「哀れ世の世にてあらましかば、當時は近衞司にてあらんずるものを。」と、宣ひけるこそ餘りの事なれ。鎌倉殿常は覺束なげにおぼして高雄の聖の許へ便宜毎に、「さても維盛卿の子息、何と候やらむ。
昔頼朝を相し給し樣に、朝の怨敵をも滅し會稽の恥をも雪むべき仁にて候か。」と尋
ね申されければ、聖の御返事には、「是は底もなき不覺仁にて候ぞ。御心安う思しめ
し候へ。」と申されけれども、鎌倉殿猶も御心ゆかずげにて「謀反をだに起さば、や
がて方人せうずる聖の御房也。但頼朝一期の程は誰か傾くべき、子孫の末ぞ知らぬ。」
と宣ひけるこそ怖しけれ、母上是を聞き給ひて、「如何にも叶まじ。はや／＼出家し給へ。」と仰ければ、六代御前十六と申し文治五年の春の比、うつくしげなる髮を肩のまはりに鋏み落し柿の衣袴に笈など拵へ聖に暇乞うて修行に出でられけり。齋藤五、齋藤六も同じ樣に出立て、御供申けり。先づ高野へ參り父の善知識したりける瀧口入道に尋合ひ御出家の次第臨終の有樣、委敷う聞給ひて、且うは其御跡もゆかしとて、熊野へ參給ひけり。濱の宮の御前にて父の渡り給ひける山なりの島を見渡して、渡らまほしくおぼしけれ共、波風向うて叶はねば、力及ばで、詠めやり給ふにも我父は何くに沈み給ひけんと、沖より寄する白波にも、問まほしくぞ思はれける。汀の沙も父の御骨やらんとなつかしうおぼしければ、涙に袖はしをれつゝ鹽くむ海士の衣ならね共、乾く間なくぞ見え給ふ。渚に一夜逗留して念佛申經讀み指の先にて沙に佛の形をかき現して、明ければ貴き僧を請じて父の御爲と供養して、作善の功徳さながら聖靈に廻向して亡者に暇申つゝ泣々都へ上られけり。

annotation.translation: In due course, when Rokudai Gozen had grown up to be fourteen or fifteen years old, her appearance became increasingly beautiful, so much so that it seemed to illuminate her surroundings. Her mother, beholding this, said, "Alas, had this been a world where one could be free, she would surely have been a lady-in-waiting in the Konoe household at this time." Such words were spoken indeed. The Kamakura Lord (Minamoto no Yoritomo) often felt uneasy and, whenever convenient, went to the High Priest at Takao, asking, "How is it that the son of Duke Iemori? Might he be a benevolent man capable of destroying our enemies like Yoritomo and washing away the shame of Kukai?" When the High Priest replied, "He is a man of boundless ignorance. Please, do not worry your heart," yet the Kamakura Lord remained unconvinced, saying, "If he were to even raise a rebellion, he would surely be destroyed by the High Priest's power. However, while Yoritomo is alive, who could possibly turn against him? As for his descendants, no one knows." Such words were spoken indeed, filled with fear. Hearing this, his mother commanded, "It is impossible to allow this. Quickly, take the tonsure." Thus, when Rokudai Gozen turned sixteen, in the spring of the fifth year of Bunji, she cut off her beautiful hair, adorned herself in a persimmon-colored robe and hakama, and prepared a pilgrim's pack, bidding farewell to the High Priest to begin her修行. Saito Go and Saito Roku also departed in the same manner to accompany her. First, they went to Koya, where they sought out Takiguchi Nyudo, her father's spiritual friend, and inquired thoroughly about the circumstances of her ordination and the manner of her death. Moreover, since they wished to follow in his footsteps, they also traveled to Kumano. At the shrine by the sea, gazing upon the islands where her father had crossed over, she longed to cross them herself, but the waves and wind were against her, and her strength was insufficient. Even when she composed a poem, thinking, "Where has my father sunk?" she felt a desire to question even the white waves rolling in from the open sea. The sands of the shore also seemed to be her father's bones, and though her sleeves were wet with tears and she was not a fisherman's daughter, she could not help but see them. Spending one night on the shore, she recited the Nembutsu, chanted sutras, and with her fingertips traced the form of Buddha in the sand. At dawn, she invited a distinguished monk, offered memorial services for her father, dedicated the merit of her good deeds to his soul, and, bidding farewell to the deceased with tears, ascended to the capital."
