text: 小松殿の御子丹後侍從忠房は八島の軍より落て行末も知らずおはせしが、紀伊國の住人湯淺權守宗重を憑んで湯淺の城にぞ籠られける。是を聞いて平家に志思ひける越中次郎兵衞、上總五郎兵衞、惡七兵衞、飛騨四郎兵衞以下の兵共著き奉由聞えしかば、伊賀、伊勢兩國の住人等、我も我もと馳集る。究竟の者共數百騎たてこもたる由聞えしかば、熊野別當、鎌倉殿より仰を蒙て兩三月が間、八箇度寄せて責戰ふ。城の内の兵共命を惜まず、防ぎければ毎度に御方追散され、熊野法師數をつくいて討れにけり。熊野別當、鎌倉殿へ飛脚を奉て當國湯淺の合戰の事兩三ケ月が間に八箇度寄て責戰ふ。されども城の内の兵共命を惜まず、防ぐ間毎度に味方おひ落されて、敵をしへたぐるに及ばず。近國二三ケ國をも給はて攻め落すべき由申たりければ、鎌倉殿「其條、國の費、人の煩なるべし。楯籠所の凶徒は定めて海山の盗人にてぞあらん。山賊海賊きびしう守護して城の口を固めて守るべし。」とぞ宣ひける。其定にしたりければ、げにも後には人一人もなかりけり。鎌倉殿謀に「小松殿の君達の一人も二人も生殘り給ひたらんをば扶け奉るべし。其故は池の禪尼の使として頼朝を流罪に申宥られしは偏に彼内府の芳恩也。」と宣ひければ、丹後侍從六波羅へ出てなのられけり。軈て關東へ下奉る。鎌倉殿對面して「都へ御上り候へ。片ほとりに思ひ當て參らする事候。」とてすかし上せ奉り追樣に人を上せて勢多の橋の邊にて切てけり。

annotation.translation: Lord Komatsu's son, the Imperial Attendant of Tango, Tadefusa, fell in the Battle of Yashima, and his fate became unknown. However, he took refuge in Yagawa Castle, relying on Yasukawa Gonnojo Muneshige, a resident of Kii Province. Hearing of this, the Chūjō Hebei, Kazusa Gōhei, Akushichi Hebei, Hida Shirohei, and other warriors of the Taira clan, who had been plotting against the Taira, gathered and reported this to the Iga and Ise residents, who then rushed to join, each claiming, "I am the one!" It was reported that several hundred mounted warriors had taken refuge there. Thus, the Kuma Bodai, receiving orders from the Kamakura Shōgun, besieged and attacked the castle eight times over the course of two or three months. The warriors inside the castle, sparing not their lives, defended themselves, yet every time they were driven back by the enemy forces, and the Kuma monks were killed one after another. The Kuma Bodai sent a messenger to the Kamakura Shōgun, reporting that over the course of two or three months, they had besieged and attacked the battle at Yagawa in Kii Province eight times. However, the warriors inside the castle, sparing not their lives, defended themselves, yet every time they were driven back by the enemy, and it became impossible to push the enemy further. It was reported that they would be granted control over two or three neighboring provinces and could be driven out, to which the Kamakura Shōgun declared, "In that case, the cost to the province and the burden on the people would be great. These besieged ruffians are surely sea and mountain bandits. They should be strictly guarded as mountain and sea robbers, and the castle gates should be fortified and defended." When this decision was made, indeed, in the end, not a single person remained. The Kamakura Shōgun schemed, saying, "If even one or two of Lord Komatsu's sons were to survive, we should support them. The reason is that Chōni of the Pond, as an envoy, had pleaded with Yoritomo to commute his exile sentence, and this was solely due to the grace of that Inner Prince." Upon hearing this, the Tango Attendant left for Rokuhara and was executed. Soon after, he descended to the Kantō region. Facing the Kamakura Shōgun, he was told, "Please ascend to the capital. There is something I wish to discuss with you." He was then invited up, and as he was being escorted, he was cut down at the side of Seta Bridge.

text: 小松殿の君達六人の外に土佐守宗實とておはしけり。三歳より大炊御門の左大臣經宗卿の養子にて異姓他人になり、武藝の道をば打棄てて文筆をのみ嗜て今年は十八に成り給ふを鎌倉殿より尋はなかりけれども、世に憚て追出されたりければ、先途を失ひ大佛の聖俊乘房のもとにおはして「我は是小松の内府の末の子に土佐守宗實と申者にて候。三歳より大炊御門左大臣經宗養子にして異姓他人になり、武藝のみちをうち捨て、文筆をのみたしなんで生年十八歳に罷成。鎌倉殿より尋らるる事は候はねども、世におそれておひ出されて候。聖の御房御弟子にせさせ給へ。」とて髻推切給ひぬ。「それも猶怖しう思食さば鎌倉へ申て、げにも罪深かるべくは何くへも遣せ。」と宣ひければ、聖最愛思ひ奉て出家せさせ奉り、東大寺の油倉と云所に暫く置奉て關東へ此由申されけり。「何樣にも見參してこそともかうもはからはめ。先づ下し奉れ。」と宣ひければ、聖力及ばで關東へ下し奉る。此人奈良を立給ひし日よりして飮食の名字を絶て湯水をも喉へいれず、足柄越て關本と云所にて遂に失給ぬ。「如何にも叶まじき道なれば。」とて思切られけるこそ怖ろしけれ。

annotation.translation: Besides the six young men of the Lord Komatsu, there was also Tosa no Kami Munenari. From the age of three, he had become the adopted son of the Left Minister of the Daigamimon, Kinenari no Kyo, and thus had become an outsider of a different surname; he had abandoned the way of martial arts and indulged only in writing. This year he had turned eighteen, and although the Lord of Kamakura had not summoned him, he had been driven out because he was afraid of the world, and had lost his path. He was present at the Great Buddha with the holy monk Shunjojo, saying, "I am the youngest son of the Inner Minister of Komatsu, named Tosa no Kami Munenari. From the age of three, I became the adopted son of the Left Minister of the Daigamimon, Kinenari, and thus became an outsider of a different surname; I abandoned the way of martial arts and indulged only in writing, and I have now reached the age of eighteen. Although the Lord of Kamakura has not summoned me, I was driven out because I was afraid of the world. Please make me your disciple, holy one." With these words, he had his topknot cut off. "If you still feel fear, tell the Lord of Kamakura; indeed, since you are deeply guilty, you may be sent anywhere." Upon hearing this, the holy monk, thinking deeply of him, had him take the tonsure, placed him for a time in a place called the Oil Warehouse of Todai-ji, and reported these circumstances to the Kantō region. "Please do not try to make any arrangements to see him in any way," he said, "first, send him down." Upon hearing this, the holy monk, unable to resist, sent him down to the Kantō region. From the day this person left Nara, he ceased all eating and drinking, even water could not pass his throat; crossing over Odawara, he finally perished at a place called Kantomoto. "Since it is a path that cannot possibly be fulfilled," he thought, and with resolve he died. How terrible it was.

text:
さる程に建久元年十一月七日鎌倉殿上洛して、同九日正二位大納言に成り給ふ。同十一日大納言の右大將を兼じ給へり。やがて兩職を辭て十二月四日關東へ下向。
建久三年三月十三日法皇崩御なりにけり。御歳六十六。瑜珈振鈴の響は其夜を限り、
一乘案誦の御聲は其曉に終ぬ。

annotation.translation: In due course, on the seventh day of the eleventh month of the first year of Kenkyu, the Lord of Kamakura ascended to Kyoto, and on the ninth day he became a Dainagon of the Second Senior Rank. On the eleventh day, he concurrently held the office of Right Captain of the Dainagon. Soon after, he resigned from both posts and descended to the Eastern Provinces on the fourth day of the twelfth month. On the thirteenth day of the third month of the third year of Kenkyu, the Retired Emperor passed away. He was sixty-six years of age. The sound of the bell-ringing at the Yogacara service lasted until that night; the sound of the Emperor's recitation of the One Vehicle sutra ended at that dawn.

text: 同六年三月十三日大佛供養有るべしとて二月中に鎌倉殿又御上洛あり。同十二日大佛殿へ參せ給ひたりけるが、梶原を召て「手かいの門の南の方に大衆なん十人を隔てゝ怪しばうだる者の見えつる。召捕て參らせよ。」と宣ひければ、梶原承てやがて召具して參りたり。鬚をば剃て髻をば切らぬ男也。「何者ぞ。」ととひ給へば、「是程運命盡果て候ぬる上はとかう申すに及ばず。是は平家の侍薩摩中務家資と申者にて候。」「それは何と思ひてかくは成りたるぞ。」「もしやとねらひ申候つる也。」「志の程はゆゝしかりけり。」とて供養果てて都へ入せ給ひて、六條河原にて切られにけり。

annotation.translation: In the sixth year, on the thirteenth day of the third month, it was said that there would be a Great Buddha offering, and during the twelfth month of the same year, the Lord of Kamakura went to the capital again. On the twelfth day, he came to the Great Buddha Hall and said, "Summon Kajiwara. A strange creature has been seen in the south of the Gate of Hand-kai, separated from the multitude of ten people. Summon and arrest it and bring it here." Kajiwara obeyed and immediately prepared the necessary items and went. It was a man who had shaved his beard but not cut his topknot. When asked, "Who are you?", he replied, "Since my fate has come to an end, there is no need to say more. I am a retainer of the Taira clan, Satsuma no Shibu, named Kazuyori." "Why did you think to do such a thing?" "I was hoping for that." "Your resolve was indeed splendid." Thus, after the offering was completed, he returned to the capital, and was beheaded at Rokujō Kawara.

text: 平家の子孫は去文治元年冬の比一つ子二つ子をのこさず腹の内をあけて見ずと云ばかりに尋取て失ひてき。今は一人もあらじと思ひしに、新中納言の末の子に伊賀大夫知忠とておはしき。平家都を落し時三歳にて棄置かれたりしを乳母の紀伊次郎兵衞爲教養ひ奉てこゝかしこに隱れありきけるが、備後國大田といふ所に忍びつゝ居たりけり。やうやう成人し給へば、郡郷の地頭守護恠しみける程に都へ上り法性寺の一の橋なる所に忍んでおはしけり。爰祖父入道相國自然の事のあらん時城廓にもせんとて堀を二重に堀て四方に竹を栽られたり。逆茂木引て晝は人音もせず、夜になれば尋常なる輩多く集て詩作り歌を讀み管絃などして遊びける程に何としてか漏れ聞えたりけん、其比人のおぢ怖れけるは一條の二位入道義泰といふ人也。其侍に後藤兵衞基清が子に新兵衞基綱「一の橋に違勅の者あり。」と聞出して、建久七年十月七日辰の一點に其勢百四五十騎一の橋へ馳せ向ひ、をめき叫んで攻め戰ふ。城の内にも三十餘人有ける者共大肩脱に袒いで竹の陰より差詰引詰さんざんに射れば、馬人多く射殺されて面を向ふべき樣もなし。「さる程に一の橋に違勅の者あり。」と聞傳へ在京の武士共我も我もと馳つどふ。程なく一二千騎に成りしかば、近邊の小家を壞ち寄せ堀を填めをめき叫んで攻入けり。城の内の兵共打物拔で走出で、或は討死する者もあり、或は痛手負て自害する者もあり。伊賀大夫知忠は生年十六歳に成られけるが、痛手負て自害し給ひたるを乳母の紀伊次郎兵衞入道膝の上に舁乘せ、涙をはら／＼と流いて高聲に十念唱へつつ腹掻切てぞ死にける。其子の兵衞太郎、兵衞次郎共に討死してんげり。城の内に三十餘人有ける者共大略討死自害して館には火を懸けたりけるを武士共馳入て手々に討ける頸共太刀長刀の先に貫ぬき二位入道殿へ馳參る。一條の大路へ車遣出して頸共實檢せらる。紀伊次郎兵衞入道の頸をば見知たる者も少々在り。伊賀大夫の頸、人爭か見知り奉べき。此人の母上は治部卿局とて八條女院に候はれけるを迎へ寄せ奉て見せ奉り給ふ。「三歳と申し時、故中納言に具せられて西國へ下りし後は生たり共死たりとも其行へを知らず、但故中納言の思出る所々のあるはさにこそ。」とて被泣けるにこそ伊賀大夫の頸とも人知てげれ。

annotation.translation: The descendants of the Heike, without leaving even one or two children behind in the winter of Bunji Year 1, were hunted down and annihilated to such an extent that it seemed they were all torn open and their insides exposed. Though I thought there would be not even a single one left, there was the youngest son of the new Chūnagon, named Iga no Daisuke Tomotada. When the Heike lost the capital, he was abandoned at the age of three, but was raised and brought up by his wet nurse, Ki no Jirō Be no Tamenori, and hid here and there. He lived in concealment at a place called Oda in Bitchū Province. As he gradually grew into adulthood, the local governors and guardians of the district and countryside marveled at him; he then ascended to the capital and hid at a place called Ichinohashi at Hōshō-ji Temple. There, his grandfather, the priest Sōkoku, when circumstances seemed to demand it, intended to turn the castle into a fortress; he dug a double moat and planted bamboo all around. He drew the sakimori, and during the day not even a human sound was heard; when night fell, many ordinary people gathered, and they spent their time composing poetry, reciting songs, and playing with musical instruments. Somehow, this leaked out and was heard. At that time, the person whom the people feared most was the retired Dainagon Jōtoku Yoshinari of the Ichijō family. Among his retainers was the son of Gotō Bē no Kiyokiya, Shinbē no Kiyetsuna, who reported, "There are those who violate the imperial decree at Ichinohashi." In the first hour of the Dragon on the seventh day of the tenth month of Kenkyū Year 7, their force of over one hundred and forty or fifty horsemen galloped toward Ichinohashi, shouting and screaming, and attacked. The more than thirty men inside the castle took off their large shoulder armor, bared their chests, and from behind the bamboo shadows, they shot arrows in volleys, driving the attackers back with great ferocity. Many of the horsemen were shot dead, and there was no way to face them. "There are those who violate the imperial decree at Ichinohashi," was reported and spread; the samurai in the capital, each shouting "I will go, I will go," galloped to join the attack. In a short while, their force grew to one or two thousand horsemen; they destroyed the small houses nearby, filled the moat, shouted and screamed, and charged into the castle. The soldiers inside the castle drew their weapons, rushed out, and some were killed in battle, while others, grievously wounded, committed suicide. Iga no Daisuke Tomotada had reached the age of sixteen; grievously wounded, he committed suicide. His wet nurse, Ki no Jirō Be, the retired priest, carried him on her lap, weeping bitterly, loudly reciting the Ten Nembutsu, and then cut open his belly before dying. His sons, Bē no Taro and Bē no Jirō, were both killed in battle. The more than thirty men inside the castle were, in general, either killed in battle or committed suicide; the mansion was set on fire. The samurai rushed in and, one by one, beheaded them, skewering the heads on the points of their long swords and short swords, and galloped to report to the Dainagon of the Ichijō family. A carriage was sent out along the main street, and the heads were inspected. There were a few people who recognized the head of Ki no Jirō Be, the retired priest. Who could fail to recognize the head of Iga no Daisuke? This person's mother, known as the Dajō-kyō no Tsubone, who had served the Hachijō Nyōgo, was summoned and shown the head. "When he was said to be three years old, he was presented to the late Chūnagon and went down to the Western Provinces; since then, whether he lived or died, I knew nothing of his whereabouts. Only the thoughts of the late Chūnagon were what I could not forget." Crying, she said these words, and thus it was that the head of Iga no Daisuke became known to the people.

text: 平家の侍越中次郎兵衞盛嗣は但馬國へ落行て氣比四郎道弘が聟に成てぞ居たりける。道弘越中次郎兵衞とは知らざりけり。されども錐嚢にたまらぬ風情にて夜になれば、しうとが馬引出いて馳引したり。海の底十四五町二十町潜などしければ、地頭守護恠しみける程に何としてか漏聞えたりけん。鎌倉殿御教書を下されけり。「但馬國の住人朝倉太郎大夫高清、平家の侍越中次郎兵衞盛嗣當國に居住の由聞食す。めし進せよ。」と仰下さる。氣比四郎は朝倉の大夫が聟なりければ、呼び寄せて「いかゞして搦めんずる。」と議するに、湯屋にてからむべしとて湯に入れてしたゝかなる者五六人おろし合せてからめんとするに、取つけば投倒され、起上れば蹴倒さる。互に身は濕たり、取もためず。されども衆力に強力叶はぬ事なれば、二三十人はと寄て太刀のみね長刀の柄にて打惱して搦捕、やがて關東へ參せたりければ、御前に引居させて事の子細を召問はる。「如何に汝は同平家の侍と云ながら故親にてあんなるに、何とてしなざりけるぞ。」「其れはあまりに平家の脆く滅て在し候間、若やとねらひ參らせ候つるなり。太刀のみの好をも征矢の尻の鐡好をも鎌倉殿の御爲とこそ拵へ持て候つれども、是程に運命盡果候ぬる上はとかう申におよび候はず。」「志の程はゆゆしかりけり。頼朝を憑まば助けて仕はんはいかに。」と仰ければ、「勇士二主に仕へず。盛嗣程の者に御心許し給ひては必ず御後悔候べし。只御恩には疾々頸を召され候へ。」と申ければ、「さらば切れ。」とて由井の濱に引出いて切てげり。ほめぬ者こそなかりけれ。

annotation.translation: Heike no samurai Echizen no Jiro Be-e Mori-tsugu fell to but to become the son-in-law of Taji no Shiro Michihiro in Tajima Province, and he resided there. He did not know that Michihiro was Echizen no Jiro Be-e. However, he was a man of such spirit that he could not be contained; when night came, his brother-in-law would bring out a horse and gallop away. He would dive into the depths of the sea, fourteen or fifteen cho, twenty cho, so the local magistrates and guardians were amazed, and when news leaked out somehow, the Lord of Kamakura issued an imperial decree: 'It has been reported that Asakura no Taro Daifu Kiyotaka, a resident of Tajima Province, is harboring Heike samurai Echizen no Jiro Be-e Mori-tsugu in this province. Arrest him.' He ordered. Since Michihiro was the son-in-law of the Daifu of Asakura, they summoned him and discussed, 'How shall we capture him?' They decided to ambush him at a bathhouse, so they lowered five or six men into the bath to entangle him. When they seized him, he threw them down; when they rose, he kicked them down. Both sides were soaked, and no one could hold back. However, since individual strength cannot match the power of many, twenty or thirty men gathered and struck him with the pommels of swords and the handles of long swords to subdue and capture him, and soon after brought him to the Kanto region. He was brought before the Lord and interrogated about the details of the matter. 'How is it that you, though a samurai of the Heike, are a relative by marriage of your former lord, yet did not serve him?' 'Because the Heike were so fragile and perished so quickly, I merely intended to offer my services.' 'Although I had prepared the sword's sharpness and the arrowhead's iron tip for the sake of the Lord of Kamakura, now that fate has thus come to an end, I could not make such a statement.' 'Your intention was indeed praiseworthy. If you had pledged loyalty to Yoritomo, you could have been saved; how could that have been?' 'A warrior serves not two masters. If you trust someone like Mori-tsugu, you will surely regret it. Simply accept my gratitude and have my neck cut.' When he said this, the Lord replied, 'Very well, then cut,' and he was taken to the shore of Yui and beheaded. There was no one who did not praise him.

text:
其比の主上は御遊をむねとせさせ給ひて、政道は一向卿の局のまゝなりければ、人の愁歎もやまず。呉王劔客を好んじかば、天下に疵を蒙る者たえず。楚王細腰を愛せしかば、宮中に飢て死する女多かりき。上の好に下は隨ふ間世の危き事を悲んで有心人々は歎きあへり。こゝに文覺本より怖き聖にて、いろふまじき事にいろひけり。二の宮は、御學問怠らせ給はず、正理を先とせさせ給ひしかば、如何にもして、此宮を位に即奉らんとはからひけれども、前右大將頼朝卿のおはせし程は叶はざりけるが、
建久十年正月十三日、頼朝卿失せ給ひしかば、やがて謀反を起さんとしける程に忽に
洩聞えて、二條猪熊の宿所に官人共つけられ召捕て八十に餘て後隱岐國へぞ流されけ
る。文覺京を出るとて、「是程老の波に望て、今日明日とも知ぬ身を、縱勅勘なりと
も都の片邊には置給はで隱岐國まで流さるる及丁冠者こそ安からね。終には文覺が流
さるゝ國へ迎へ申さんずるものを。」と、申けるこそ怖しけれ。此君は餘に毬杖の玉
を愛せさせ給ひければ文覺かやうに惡口申ける也。されば承久に御謀反起させ給ひて、
國こそ多けれ、隱岐國へうつされ給ひけるこそ不思議なれ。彼國にても文覺が亡靈荒て、
常は御物語申けるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: At that time, the Emperor made it his custom to play games, and since governance was entirely in the hands of the minister's household, people's sighs of lamentation did not cease. Because King Wu of Wu favored swordsmen, many in the world suffered harm. Because King Zhuang of Chu loved slender waists, many women in the palace starved to death. Since those below follow the preferences of those above, the world's dangerous affairs caused the thoughtful people to sigh in sorrow. Here, Monjo, who was originally a terrifying saint, spoke harshly about things that were not harsh. The Second Prince did not neglect his studies, and he made it his priority to uphold justice; thus, he plotted in every way to place this Prince on the throne, but it did not come to pass to the extent that the former Right Great Captain, the Lord Yoritomo, had done. On the thirteenth day of the first month of the tenth year of Kenkyu, when the Lord Yoritomo passed away, he was immediately suspected of plotting rebellion; suddenly, the news leaked, and he was surrounded by officials at the residence of Ni-no-miya Inokuma, arrested, and exiled to Oki Province along with more than eighty others. When Monjo left the capital, he said, 'At this stage of old age, with waves of uncertainty, I do not know my fate for today or tomorrow. Even if it is by imperial decree, it is not right to leave me in a corner of the capital; I must be exiled to Oki Province. The most fitting thing would be to welcome Monjo to the very country to which he is exiled.' How terrifying it was when he spoke thus! This Prince, because he loved the jade of the ball-and-mallet game so much, caused Monjo to speak such harsh words. Therefore, during the Jokyō period, he was made to rise in rebellion; although there were many provinces, it is strange that he was transferred to Oki Province. Even in that country, it is said that Monjo's spirit was restless and often told him stories.

text: さる程に六代御前は、三位禪師とて、高雄に行ひすましておはしけるを、「さる人の子也。さる人の弟子なり。首をば剃たりとも、心をばよも剃じ。」とて、鎌倉殿より頻に申されければ、安判官資兼に仰せて召捕て、關東へぞ下されける。駿河國の住人岡邊權守泰綱に仰せて、田越河にて、切れてけり。十二の歳より三十に餘まで保ちけるは、偏に長谷の觀音の御利生とぞ聞えし。それよりしてこそ平家の子孫は永く絶にけれ。

annotation.translation: Thus, the Sixth Emperor, who was known as the Third Rank Zen Priest, had gone to Takao and was residing there. He was told, 'He is a man's son; he is a man's disciple. Even if his head is shaved, his heart shall not be shaved.' Because this was frequently reported from the Kamakura Lord, he was ordered by the Anno Judge Sukechika to be summoned and arrested, and was sent down to the Kanto region. He was ordered to be cut down at the Tagoe River by Okabe no Gon no Kami Yasutsuna, a resident of Suruga Province. He had maintained this state from the age of twelve to over thirty; it was heard that this was entirely due to the merit of the Hasedera Kannon. From that time on, the descendants of the Taira family were utterly extinguished.
